13-14.label: Foundation
13-14.emphasis: ~70% technical: ball mastery, first touch, 1v1, SSGs; introduce heading & GK streams

15-16.label: Development
15-16.emphasis: Technical + tactical principles, position-specific work, supervised strength intro

17-19.label: Performance
17-19.emphasis: Position specialisation, game model, set pieces, physical loading, senior-football mirror

drills.name: Ball Mastery: Sole Rolls & Inside Taps
drills.description: Stationary and moving touches using sole rolls, inside-outside touches and toe taps. Foundation routine for close control, performed in a small grid per player.
coaching_points: Keep head up between touches
Light, frequent touches - ball stays within one step
Work both feet equally

rubric.description: 1 = heavy touches; the ball leaves the one-step zone; 3 = light, frequent touches with the ball inside one step on most reps; 5 = soft, quick touches with the ball always within one step, using sole, inside and toe taps cleanly
1 = clearly weaker on one foot; rhythm breaks often; 3 = both feet used and the rhythm holds for most of the block; 5 = both feet equally sharp and the rhythm holds for the whole block
1 = eyes on the ball all the time; 3 = looks up between touches on most reps; 5 = head up on most touches while keeping full control

drills.progression: Add a turn every 10 touches, then perform while jogging through a gate course.
drills.video_note: Front and side view of a player performing the full routine at slow then full tempo.

drills.name: Ball Mastery: V-Pulls & L-Turns
drills.description: Turning repertoire using V-pulls and L-turns to change direction away from imaginary pressure.
coaching_points: Push the ball forward before dragging back
Accelerate out of the turn
Turn both directions equally

rubric.description: 1 = ball runs away or the turn is slow; 3 = ball stays close through the pull or turn on most reps; 5 = tidy, quick V-pull and L-turn with the ball under control every time
1 = turns well to one side only; 3 = turns both ways, the weaker side a little slower; 5 = both directions equally clean
1 = stops after the turn; 3 = pushes out of the turn on most reps; 5 = pushes out and accelerates away on every rep

drills.progression: Perform against a passive defender who shows a side; execute the turn away from pressure.
drills.video_note: Close-up of footwork plus full-body view showing the acceleration after each turn.

drills.name: Step-overs & Scissors (Static to Moving)
drills.description: Step-over and scissors technique broken down statically, then performed while dribbling between cones.
coaching_points: Sell the fake with shoulder and hip drop
Touch out with the opposite foot after the fake
Build speed gradually - technique first

rubric.description: 1 = foot passes over the ball with no body movement; 3 = shoulder and hip drop sell the move on most reps; 5 = a full-body fake that would move a defender, every rep
1 = weak touch out, or uses the same foot; 3 = touches out with the opposite foot on most reps; 5 = sharp touch out with the opposite foot and a burst of pace, every rep
1 = loses the ball as soon as speed rises; 3 = holds the technique at jogging pace; 5 = holds the technique at near full pace between cones

drills.progression: Execute at a mannequin, then against a passive defender in a 1v1 gate game.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion breakdown of the footwork, then game-speed application.

drills.name: Cruyff Turn Mastery
drills.description: Repetition of the Cruyff turn on both feet, first static then on the move, finishing with a pass or shot after the turn.
coaching_points: Plant foot beside the ball
Drag with the inside of the foot behind the standing leg
Head up immediately after the turn

rubric.description: 1 = drags the ball past the standing foot or loses it; 3 = plant foot beside the ball and a clean drag on most reps; 5 = smooth, fast turn every rep
1 = looks down after the turn; 3 = head up within a touch or two on most reps; 5 = head up straight after the turn and picks the pass or shot
1 = turns well off one foot only; 3 = both feet, the weaker side slower; 5 = both feet equally clean, standing and moving

drills.progression: Use the turn to beat a defender and finish on goal.
drills.video_note: Front and rear angles at slow motion; emphasise the disguised shape before the turn.

drills.name: Juggling Foundations
drills.description: Progressive juggling: bounce-juggle, two-touch per foot, then continuous keep-ups with feet only.
coaching_points: Relaxed ankle, toe slightly up
Keep the ball below knee height to start
Set personal records and log them

rubric.description: 1 = ball goes high and the ankle is stiff; 3 = relaxed ankle and the ball below knee height on most touches; 5 = soft, low, relaxed touches with the ball always under control
1 = fewer than 5 touches in a row; 3 = 10 to 20 touches in a row; 5 = 30 or more touches in a row, repeated across attempts

drills.progression: Move to alternating feet, then feet-thigh-head sequences.
drills.video_note: Demonstration of the full progression ladder with target numbers per level.
drills.safety_note: Head juggling counts as heading. FA youth heading guidance: no heading in training under U12; at U13 no more than 5 headers per player per session, and from U14 no more than 10, with one heading session a week at most. Keep head touches to the session limit, use a dry ball at low pressure, and count them.

drills.name: Juggling Advanced: Alternating & Weak Foot
drills.description: Advanced juggling patterns: strict left-right alternation, weak-foot-only blocks, feet-thigh-head circuits, and low-keep-up control.
coaching_points: Hips square and balanced
Every touch controlled, not reactive
Weak foot sets are non-negotiable

rubric.description: 1 = ball bounces about with no pattern; 3 = controlled patterns with hips square on most sets; 5 = every touch placed on purpose, hips square and balanced
1 = weak-foot sets break inside 5 touches; 3 = strict left-right alternation for 10 or more touches; 5 = strict alternation and weak-foot-only sets of 20 or more touches

drills.progression: Add movement (walk a line while juggling) or partner juggling with limited touches.
drills.video_note: Examples of each pattern with target rep counts per age band.
drills.safety_note: Head juggling counts as heading. FA youth heading guidance: no more than 10 headers per player per session and one heading session a week at most (U14 to U18). Count head touches with any other heading in the session. Use a dry ball at low pressure.

drills.name: Wall-Pass First Touch
drills.description: Pass against a wall and control the rebound: inside-foot cushion, outside-of-foot across body, and directed first touch into gates left and right.
coaching_points: Open body shape before the ball arrives
Cushion - don't stop dead
Touch must take you toward your next action

rubric.description: 1 = ball bounces off the foot; 3 = cushioned touch on most balls; 5 = soft touch with the right surface every time
1 = faces the wall with shoulders square; 3 = opens the body before the ball arrives on most reps; 5 = opens early every rep and knows the next gate before the ball returns
1 = first touch rarely reaches a gate; 3 = reaches the chosen gate on most reps; 5 = reaches the chosen gate every rep, even when the call changes

drills.progression: Randomise gates with coloured cones or a partner call; react and adapt the touch.
drills.video_note: Overhead or 45-degree view showing touch direction into each gate.

drills.name: First Touch Out of the Air
drills.description: Self-serve or partner-serve: control balls from height using foot, thigh, chest, and combinations (thigh-chest-feet), finishing with a pass to a target.
coaching_points: Watch the ball onto the surface
Withdraw the surface on contact to kill the pace
Second touch plays forward

rubric.description: 1 = ball bounces away; 3 = right surface and a softened touch on most balls; 5 = surface withdraws and the ball dies at the feet every time
1 = pass to the target rarely finds it; 3 = second touch plays forward to the target on most balls; 5 = control and pass to the target in two touches nearly every time
1 = controls well with one surface only; 3 = controls with foot, thigh and chest on most balls; 5 = controls cleanly with every surface and combination

drills.progression: Add a passive presser so the first touch must beat pressure.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion of each surface controlling the ball; show bad vs. good cushion.

drills.name: Receiving on the Half-Turn
drills.description: Midfielder receives from a server with a passive defender behind; scans, receives on the back foot on the half-turn, and plays forward.
coaching_points: Check shoulder before the pass travels
Side-on body shape - see both goals
Receive on the back foot to face forward

rubric.description: 1 = receives square and loses the ball; 3 = receives on the back foot on most reps; 5 = clean half-turn on the back foot every rep
1 = always turns, even under pressure; 3 = turns or sets correctly on most reps; 5 = reads the defender and picks turn or set nearly every rep
1 = forward pass rarely completed; 3 = forward pass completed on most reps; 5 = turn and forward pass completed nearly every rep
1 = never checks over the shoulder; 3 = checks before the pass travels on most reps; 5 = checks early on every rep

drills.progression: Make the defender live; receiver decides turn or set based on pressure.
drills.video_note: Midfield camera angle showing the scan, shape, and first touch in sequence.

drills.name: Rondo 4v2 / 5v2 Foundations
drills.description: Classic possession rondo in a small grid. Two-touch limit, defenders swap after a set number of passes or an interception.
coaching_points: Create passing lines - constant angles
Play the way you face
Defenders press together, split passes

rubric.description: 1 = more than two touches; ball loose; 3 = keeps the two-touch limit on most passes; 5 = clean, quick one- and two-touch passing
1 = passers stand still; 3 = move to create a passing line on most possessions; 5 = constant angles; the ball never gets stuck
1 = plays into the defenders' reach; 3 = finds the free player on most passes; 5 = plays the way they face and splits the defenders nearly every pass
1 = defenders chase alone; 3 = defenders press together on most possessions; 5 = defenders press as a pair and split passes every time

drills.progression: Reduce to one-touch, shrink the grid, or add a transition element (break out to a target).
drills.video_note: High angle showing spacing, body shape, and one/two-touch rhythm.

drills.name: Rondo with Transition (Win & Switch)
drills.description: Two connected grids: on winning the ball, defenders play it to the far grid and sprint to support - trains transition in both directions.
coaching_points: First thought after winning: forward
Losing team reacts instantly to counter-press
Speed of the switch wins the transition

rubric.description: 1 = players bunch and give no angles; 3 = open angles in the grid on most possessions; 5 = constant angles, and the switch team spreads to support at once
1 = loses the ball or plays backward after winning it; 3 = plays forward into the far grid on most wins; 5 = first pass after winning is forward and quick, nearly every time
1 = silent; 3 = calls 'switch' or 'press' on most turnovers; 5 = clear calls from the whole group each time
1 = slow to react after losing the ball; 3 = reacts within a second on most turnovers; 5 = reacts at once on nearly every turnover

drills.progression: Add a counter-pressing constraint: ball must be recovered within 5 seconds for a bonus point.
drills.video_note: Wide angle capturing both grids and the sprint transition between them.

drills.name: Passing Accuracy Gates
drills.description: Pass through cone gates at 5/10/15m with both feet. Track hits out of 10 per distance per foot for measurable progress.
coaching_points: Non-kicking foot beside the ball pointing at target
Strike the midline of the ball for flat passes
Follow through low toward the gate

rubric.description: 1 = non-kicking foot behind or wide; no follow-through; 3 = plant foot beside the ball and a low follow-through on most passes; 5 = sound technique on every pass at every distance
1 = 0 to 4 of 10 through the 10 m gate; 3 = 5 to 7 of 10 through the 10 m gate; 5 = 8 or more of 10 through the 10 m gate
1 = weaker foot is 4 or more hits behind the stronger foot; 3 = weaker foot within 2 to 3 hits of the stronger foot; 5 = weaker foot within 1 hit of the stronger foot

drills.progression: Add a moving ball, a one-touch limit, or a time challenge per gate set.
drills.video_note: Side-on slow motion of the strike; score sheet showing hit targets per foot.

drills.name: Short Passing Technique (Inside, Driven, Lofted)
drills.description: Pair passing ladders focusing on three pass types: inside-foot push pass, driven pass with laces-low, and clipped lofted pass.
coaching_points: Check shoulder before receiving
Weight of pass: firm enough to arrive flat
Communicate on every ball

rubric.description: 1 = the same technique for every pass type; 3 = inside, driven and lofted passes look different and correct on most reps; 5 = correct technique for each pass type every rep
1 = passes arrive bouncing or too slow; 3 = firm passes arrive flat on most reps; 5 = right weight to the partner's front foot every pass
1 = never checks before receiving; 3 = checks the shoulder before receiving on most passes; 5 = checks early every time and receives facing the next pass
1 = silent; 3 = calls for the ball on most passes; 5 = clear, early calls on every pass

drills.progression: Introduce a defender between the pair; pass selection must beat the block.
drills.video_note: One clip per pass type, slow motion on contact point and ball flight.

drills.name: One-Twos / Wall Passes in Motion
drills.description: Pairs move up a channel playing one-twos around mannequins, finishing with a pass into a mini-goal or to a target player.
coaching_points: Pass and move immediately - never admire
Return pass into the runner's path
Angle of support from the wall player

rubric.description: 1 = heavy touch and a poor pass; 3 = clean touch and a firm pass on most reps; 5 = one- and two-touch passing at pace every rep
1 = stands and watches the pass; 3 = moves straight after passing on most reps; 5 = passes and moves at once every rep
1 = return pass goes behind the runner; 3 = return pass goes into the runner's path on most reps; 5 = perfect weight into the runner's stride every rep

drills.progression: Add a live defender on the wall player; recognise when to spin instead.
drills.video_note: Overhead view of the channel pattern with timing of the return pass highlighted.

drills.name: Third-Man Passing Patterns
drills.description: Three-player patterns where the free player is the third man: A-to-B, B sets, A plays C running beyond. Rotating roles.
coaching_points: Set passes must be soft and angled
Third man times the run off the set
Scan to find the free player, not the obvious one

rubric.description: 1 = set pass is hard or square; 3 = soft, angled set on most reps; 5 = perfect set every rep
1 = third man runs too early or too late; 3 = third man runs off the set on most reps; 5 = every run timed to the set
1 = plays to the obvious player; 3 = finds the free player on most reps; 5 = finds the free player early every time
1 = ball goes behind the runner; 3 = ball goes into the runner's path on most reps; 5 = ball goes into stride and behind the line every rep

drills.progression: Add defenders on the set player; extend to four-player patterns through the thirds.
drills.video_note: Tactical cam with player labels; freeze-frames on the moment of the set.

drills.name: Combination Play Circuit (Overlap, Underlap, Give-and-Go)
drills.description: Rotating circuit of three combination stations: give-and-go, overlap cross, underlap through-ball, each finishing on goal.
coaching_points: Trigger movements off the pass, not before it
Crosser delivers early on the overlap
Underlap runner attacks the half-space

rubric.description: 1 = loose touches; 3 = clean passing at pace on most reps; 5 = clean passing at pace at every station
1 = moves before the pass; 3 = moves off the pass on most reps; 5 = triggers every move off the pass
1 = picks the wrong combination; 3 = picks the right pattern on most reps; 5 = picks the right pattern every time
1 = cross or through-ball rarely finds the runner; 3 = finds the runner on most reps; 5 = delivers early and accurately, and the move ends in a shot

drills.progression: Remove mannequins and play the same combinations against a live back line.
drills.video_note: One clip per combination from a wide angle, run twice at game speed.

drills.name: Long-Range Distribution: Driven, Diagonal, Switch
drills.description: Hitting 25-40m passes into target zones: driven flat passes, lofted diagonals, and crossfield switches to a receiving player.
coaching_points: Lock the ankle, strike through the bottom half for flight
Body over the ball for driven passes
Receiver checks away then comes to the flight

rubric.description: 1 = ball is flat or bounces; 3 = locked ankle and good flight on most strikes; 5 = driven, lofted and switch strikes are each clean
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 reach the target zone; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 reach the target zone; 5 = 8 or more of 10 reach the target zone, also under pressure
1 = plays long when short is better; 3 = picks the right ball on most reps; 5 = switches play at the right moment nearly every time

drills.progression: Add a presser on the passer and a defender on the receiver; must complete under pressure.
drills.video_note: Side view of technique plus wide view of ball flight and zone accuracy.

drills.name: Build-Up Through the Thirds (Pattern Play)
drills.description: Structured pattern: GK/back line build through midfield into the final third against passive then active pressure, rehearsing your game model's rotations.
coaching_points: Create width and depth immediately
Midfielders play between lines, side-on
Recognise the trigger to go direct vs. recycle

rubric.description: 1 = players bunch and block passing lanes; 3 = good width and depth on most phases; 5 = shape matches the game model through all three thirds
1 = forces the pass; 3 = picks direct or recycle well on most possessions; 5 = recognises the trigger early and chooses right nearly every time
1 = receives without looking; 3 = checks before receiving on most passes; 5 = scans early and receives side-on between the lines
1 = silent; 3 = calls for the ball and gives short instructions on most possessions; 5 = constant, clear talk that helps the team move together

drills.progression: Progress to 7v5 then full opposition with counter-attacking consequences on loss.
drills.video_note: Full-pitch tactical cam with freeze-frames on each rotation trigger.

drills.name: Cone Slalom: Tight Control at Speed
drills.description: Dribble through a tight cone slalom using both feet and varied surfaces (inside, outside, sole), finishing with a strike on goal.
coaching_points: Small touches - one per stride in tight zones
Knees bent, body over the ball
Accelerate out of the last cone

rubric.description: 1 = ball leaves the cone gaps; 3 = ball stays close with one touch per stride on most cones; 5 = tight touches through every gap at pace
1 = one foot or one surface only; 3 = both feet and two surfaces on most runs; 5 = both feet and all surfaces clean on every run
1 = loses speed and shoots wide; 3 = accelerates after the last cone and hits the target on most runs; 5 = accelerates cleanly and shoots on target every run

drills.progression: Time the runs and set personal bests; shrink cone spacing as times improve.
drills.video_note: Overhead view of the slalom line with touch-count visible; slow-motion footwork insert.

drills.name: Speed Dribbling 20-30m with Finish
drills.description: Max-speed dribble over 20-30m into a finish. Trains big touches in space, head-up running, and composing for the shot.
coaching_points: Push the ball 2-3m ahead and sprint
Touch with laces/outside at speed
Last touch sets the shot - don't over-run it

rubric.description: 1 = touches too short or too long; 3 = pushes the ball 2 to 3 m ahead on most touches; 5 = big touches in space with a sprint rhythm and the ball under control
1 = eyes on the ball; 3 = looks up often; 5 = scans the goal and keeper while running at full speed
1 = overruns the ball into the shot; 3 = last touch sets up the shot on most runs; 5 = last touch sets the shot every run, on target

drills.progression: Add a recovering defender chasing from behind or from the side.
drills.video_note: Side-tracking shot showing stride and touch rhythm at full speed.

drills.name: 1v1 Moves Library (Step-over, Matthews, Elastico, Body Feint)
drills.description: Technique block learning four core 1v1 moves unopposed, then applied at mannequins with an exit gate and finish.
coaching_points: Sell every move with the body, not just the feet
Change of pace after the move is the real weapon
Master 2 moves fully rather than 6 poorly

rubric.description: 1 = moves done with the feet only; 3 = shoulder and hip sell the move on most reps; 5 = every move uses the whole body and looks real
1 = no change of pace after the move; 3 = accelerates away on most reps; 5 = clear change of pace through the exit gate every rep
1 = tries all four moves badly; 3 = two moves done well; 5 = two moves done well on both feet at pace

drills.progression: Moves applied against a live defender in gate games.
drills.video_note: One slow-motion clip per move from the defender's eye line, then game-speed.

drills.name: Shielding & Protecting the Ball
drills.description: Back-to-pressure shielding: arm length distance, low centre of gravity, using arms legally, rolling the defender to escape.
coaching_points: Body between ball and opponent at all times
Feel the defender - roll off the side they lean on
Wide base, strong core

rubric.description: 1 = ball ahead of the body; arms flap; 3 = body between ball and opponent on most reps, low and wide; 5 = strong low base and legal arm use every rep
1 = loses the ball when pushed; 3 = feels the defender and adjusts on most reps; 5 = reads the defender's push and rolls off it every rep
1 = holds the ball for under 3 seconds; 3 = holds the ball for about 5 seconds on most reps; 5 = holds the ball for 8 or more seconds and escapes with it

drills.progression: Add a support player; shield then bounce pass out of pressure.
drills.video_note: Rear angle showing body positioning and the roll escape.

drills.name: 1v1 to Goal from Varied Angles
drills.description: Attacker vs defender to goal from three starting pictures: facing the defender, receiving with back to goal, and attacking from the flank.
coaching_points: Attack the defender's front foot
If they drop - shoot; if they lunge - beat them
Finish every rep properly

rubric.description: 1 = always dribbles, whatever the defender does; 3 = shoots or beats the defender as the defender reacts, on most reps; 5 = reads the defender and picks the right action nearly every rep
1 = slow or heavy touches when attacking; 3 = attacks the front foot and beats the defender on most reps; 5 = beats the defender with a quick, clean move on most reps
1 = rarely finishes; 3 = finishes on most reps; 5 = finishes properly every rep
1 = jogs the attack; 3 = attacks at speed on most reps; 5 = attacks at full speed, inside the time limit

drills.progression: Add a time limit (6 seconds) or a recovering second defender.
drills.video_note: One clip per starting picture, attacking-camera angle.

drills.name: Tight-Area 1v1/2v2 Grid Games
drills.description: Small-grid games (10x10m) where dribbling past a player scores points. Encourages improvisation and close control under real pressure.
coaching_points: Head up - know where the space is
Use feints to unbalance before committing
If blocked, protect and recycle

rubric.description: 1 = loses the ball when closed in; 3 = keeps the ball close under pressure on most reps; 5 = close control and quick feints under pressure
1 = dribbles into trouble; 3 = chooses when to beat or protect on most reps; 5 = chooses right nearly every time
1 = head down; 3 = looks up often; 5 = knows where the space is on every rep
1 = low effort; 3 = works hard through the game; 5 = high tempo and constant movement

drills.progression: Reduce grid size or add a neutral player creating constant overloads.
drills.video_note: High-angle clip of a 60-second round showing multiple duel outcomes.

drills.name: Transition Dribbling: Attack Space After Winning the Ball
drills.description: Possession game where the team winning the ball must dribble or carry it into an end zone within 5 seconds to score.
coaching_points: First touch after regain goes forward into space
Carry at speed to commit defenders
Teammates sprint beyond the ball

rubric.description: 1 = heavy first touch; 3 = first touch forward on most regains; 5 = first touch forward into space every regain
1 = dribbles when a pass is on; 3 = picks dribble or pass well on most regains; 5 = picks right nearly every regain
1 = rarely reaches the end zone; 3 = reaches the end zone within 5 seconds on most regains; 5 = reaches the end zone within 5 seconds nearly every time
1 = slow carry; 3 = carries at speed; 5 = carries at full speed while teammates sprint beyond the ball

drills.progression: Add a counter-goal option so the carrier must choose: dribble or play forward.
drills.video_note: Wide angle with a visible countdown from the regain.

drills.name: Striking Technique: Laces & Side-Foot (Unopposed)
drills.description: Blocked repetition of the two core strikes: laces (power) and side-foot (placement) from static and rolling balls into targeted goal zones.
coaching_points: Ankle locked, toe down for laces; open hip for side-foot
Head steady over the ball at contact
Land on the shooting foot on power strikes

rubric.description: 1 = toe-poke, or hips closed; 3 = locked ankle for laces and open hip for side-foot on most strikes; 5 = clean, repeatable contact on both strikes
1 = one strike only, and form breaks with a rolling ball; 3 = both strikes hold their shape from static and rolling balls; 5 = both strikes hold form from static, rolling and after a dribble
1 = 0 to 2 of 10 in the target zone; 3 = 4 to 6 of 10 in the target zone; 5 = 7 or more of 10 in the target zone

drills.progression: Strike after a dribble or off a rebound; keep the zone targets.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion contact frames for both techniques, side and rear view.

drills.name: Volleys & Half-Volleys
drills.description: Served balls finished as full volleys and half-volleys. Focus on timing, balance, and keeping the strike down.
coaching_points: Eyes on the ball until contact
Knee over the ball to keep it down
Let the ball come - don't lunge

rubric.description: 1 = lunges, and the ball flies high; 3 = eyes on the ball and knee over it on most volleys; 5 = balanced, low, clean contact on full and half volleys
1 = misses or mistimes most balls; 3 = connects with most balls; 5 = meets the ball at the right moment every time
1 = few on target; 3 = on target on most volleys; 5 = low and on target on nearly every volley

drills.progression: Finish from crosses delivered at varied heights and speeds.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion of body shape at contact; show the common lean-back error.

drills.name: Finishing from Cutbacks
drills.description: Wide player drives to the byline and cuts the ball back; striker makes a curved arriving run and finishes first or second time.
coaching_points: Delay the run - arrive as the ball arrives
Attack the space at the penalty spot, not the ball line
Open body to finish back across goal

rubric.description: 1 = arrives early or late; 3 = arrives as the ball arrives on most reps; 5 = every run arrives with the ball
1 = runs to the ball line; 3 = attacks the penalty spot on most reps; 5 = attacks the penalty spot every rep
1 = closed body; 3 = opens the body to finish across goal on most reps; 5 = every finish with an open body and clean contact
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 on target; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 on target; 5 = 7 or more of 10 on target

drills.progression: Add a defender tracking the runner and a GK starting centrally.
drills.video_note: Wide-angle clip with the runner's arc highlighted; freeze on the arrival moment.

drills.name: Finishing After Combination Play
drills.description: Striker links with midfielders (set, spin, one-two) before finishing. Rotating roles, both feet.
coaching_points: Sharp one-touch set with the correct weight
Explode after the set - separation wins the shot
Finish across the GK when in doubt

rubric.description: 1 = heavy or badly weighted set; 3 = one-touch set with the right weight on most reps; 5 = perfect set every rep
1 = stays after the set; 3 = explodes after the set on most reps; 5 = explodes and gains separation every rep
1 = shoots at the keeper; 3 = finishes across the keeper on most reps; 5 = picks the right finish every time
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 on target; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 on target; 5 = 7 or more of 10 on target, with both feet

drills.progression: Replace mannequins with live defenders and a limited touch count.
drills.video_note: Two angles: behind-goal and tactical wide, at game speed.

drills.name: First-Time Finishes from Crosses
drills.description: Near-post, far-post and cutback zones attacked with first-time finishes from crossed deliveries. Three rotating stations.
coaching_points: Near post: steal in front of the defender
Far post: arrive at the back stick, don't wait
Adjust feet early - no stutter steps

rubric.description: 1 = stutters or waits for the ball; 3 = arrives with the ball on most crosses; 5 = arrives at the right moment every cross
1 = ball-watches or runs to the wrong post; 3 = steals in front at the near post or arrives at the back stick on most reps; 5 = runs to the right zone every rep
1 = hesitant touch; 3 = first-time contact on most crosses; 5 = first-time clean contact every time
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 on target; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 on target; 5 = 7 or more of 10 on target

drills.progression: Add defenders contesting the cross and a second-ball rule for rebounds.
drills.video_note: Overhead diagram of the three zones plus live clips of each finish type.

drills.name: Finishing Under Pressure (1v1 GK, Recovering Defender)
drills.description: Striker receives to goal with a defender recovering from the side/behind and a live GK. Decision and composure under chase pressure.
coaching_points: First touch away from the recovery angle
Decide early: round, slot, or dink
Stay composed - don't snatch at it

rubric.description: 1 = decides late; 3 = picks round, slot or dink early on most reps; 5 = picks early and right nearly every rep
1 = first touch costs time; 3 = first touch away from the recovery angle on most reps; 5 = every first touch away from the angle
1 = snatches at the shot; 3 = composed finish on most reps; 5 = composed finish every rep
1 = jogs the run; 3 = good pace on most reps; 5 = full pace with the defender chasing

drills.progression: Reduce the time window or start the defender closer.
drills.video_note: Chase-cam style angle showing the defender closing and the finish decision.

drills.name: Shooting Circuit: Angles & Distances
drills.description: Four rotating stations: edge-of-box strike, angled drive, dribble-and-shoot, rebound finish. High-repetition volume block.
coaching_points: Quality over volume - full focus each rep
Scan the GK position before striking
Follow in every shot for rebounds

rubric.description: 1 = rushed and loose; 3 = good contact on most shots; 5 = good contact every rep at every station
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 on target; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 on target; 5 = 7 or more of 10 on target across stations
1 = shoots without looking; 3 = checks the keeper's position on most shots; 5 = checks every shot and picks the open side
1 = does not follow in; 3 = follows in on most shots; 5 = follows in on every shot

drills.name: Weak-Foot Finishing Block
drills.description: Dedicated weak-foot-only finishing from short range, gradually extending distance. Tracked separately in the player's profile.
coaching_points: Accept slower progress - rebuild the technique properly
Extra reps, shorter distances, cleaner contact
Log weak-foot scores separately to see the trend

rubric.description: 1 = poor contact and a closed body; 3 = clean contact from short range on most strikes; 5 = clean contact at the longer range too
1 = avoids the weaker foot; 3 = uses the weaker foot for most reps; 5 = weak-foot score is close to the stronger foot
1 = fewer than 3 of 10 on target; 3 = 5 or 6 of 10 on target; 5 = 8 or more of 10 on target, as the distance grows

drills.progression: Weak-foot finishing from crosses and cutbacks; then a mixed-feet randomised service.

drills.name: Heading Technique Foundations
drills.description: Self-toss and partner-serve heading: forehead contact, eyes open, neck firm, heading through the ball. Standing then jumping.
coaching_points: Contact on the forehead hairline
Attack the ball - don't let it hit you
Power comes from the neck and back arch, arms for balance

rubric.description: 1 = ball hits the face or top of head; eyes shut; 3 = forehead contact and a firm neck on most headers; 5 = clean forehead contact, eyes open, body behind the ball, every header
1 = jumps early or late; 3 = meets the ball at the highest point on most headers; 5 = meets the ball at the highest point nearly every time
1 = direction rarely goes where intended; 3 = goes to the target area on most headers; 5 = accurate to the target nearly every header

drills.progression: Head to targets, then head under light defensive pressure.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion front view of contact point and neck position.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Keep service short (thrown or passed, under 10 m), not long kicks, and avoid headers after a long run-up. Use a dry ball at low pressure. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session. Players under U14 follow the lower limit of 5 headers, unopposed (see he-006 and he-007).

drills.name: Defensive vs. Attacking Heading
drills.description: Contrast block: defensive headers (height, distance, wide) vs. attacking headers (downward, powered toward corners).
coaching_points: Defensive: head under the ball, up and away
Attacking: head down on top of the ball toward goal
Jump timing: meet it at the highest point

rubric.description: 1 = the same contact for both header types; 3 = defensive (under, up and away) and attacking (over, down) look different on most headers; 5 = both contact points clean every header
1 = jumps early or late; 3 = meets the ball at the highest point on most headers; 5 = meets the ball at the highest point nearly every header

1 = defensive headers drop short or stay central; 3 = defensive headers gain height and distance, and attacking headers go down, on most headers; 5 = every header does its job: clear and wide, or down toward goal

drills.progression: Contest both types from crossed deliveries with a live opponent.
drills.video_note: Split-screen of the two contact shapes.

Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session.

drills.name: Heading from Crosses (Near-Post Flick, Far-Post Power)
drills.description: Timed runs to attack crosses: near-post flick-ons and far-post power headers, from both flanks.
coaching_points: Curve the run to attack the ball, not wait for it
Near post: glance across; far post: head down and back across
Hold the finish - follow the rebound

rubric.description: 1 = waits for the ball; 3 = run times to the cross on most reps; 5 = curved run is timed to every cross
1 = poor contact; 3 = near-post glance or far-post header down on most reps; 5 = both headers clean
1 = misses the target; 3 = on target on most headers; 5 = on target nearly every header and follows the rebound
1 = runs straight at the ball; 3 = curves the run on most reps; 5 = curved run to the right zone every time

drills.progression: Add a marking defender and GK communication element.
drills.video_note: Wide angle showing run timing plus a behind-goal angle of contact.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session. Use short or medium crosses and keep headers to the session limit.

drills.name: Aerial Duels 1v1/2v2
drills.description: Contested aerial balls from serves and long kicks: attackers head at goal, defenders head clear. Points for wins.
coaching_points: Get goalside/attack side of your opponent
Jump through the line of the ball
Win the second ball after every duel

rubric.description: 1 = loses the goal-side or attack-side position; 3 = gets the right side on most duels; 5 = gets the right side nearly every duel
1 = jumps late; 3 = jumps through the line of the ball on most duels; 5 = jumps through the line nearly every duel
1 = poor contact; 3 = clean contact on most duels; 5 = clean contact every duel, without arms
1 = does not follow the knockdown; 3 = wins the second ball on most duels; 5 = goes for the second ball every duel

drills.progression: Play 2v2 with knockdowns - second-ball finishes count double.
drills.video_note: Side view showing take-off timing and body contact rules.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Keep service short (thrown or passed, under 10 m), not long kicks, and avoid headers after a long run-up. Use a dry ball at low pressure. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session. Contested headers only at U15 and older. No use of arms.

drills.name: Second-Ball Games
drills.description: Conditioned game starting from an aerial ball: points for winning the knockdown and for the team that controls the second ball.
coaching_points: Anticipate where the knockdown lands
Attack the second ball at full speed
Compact shape behind the duel

rubric.description: 1 = ball-watches; 3 = moves toward the likely landing zone on most duels; 5 = covers the landing zone and keeps a compact shape behind the duel every time
1 = reacts after the ball lands; 3 = reads the knockdown on most duels; 5 = anticipates the knockdown early nearly every duel
1 = jogs to second balls; 3 = sprints to most second balls; 5 = attacks every second ball at full speed
1 = silent; 3 = calls 'mine' or 'second' on most duels; 5 = clear calls on every duel

drills.progression: Chain to a quick finish: goal only counts within 8 seconds of winning the second ball.
drills.video_note: Wide tactical angle showing duel plus second-ball reactions.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Keep service short (thrown or passed, under 10 m), not long kicks, and avoid headers after a long run-up. Use a dry ball at low pressure. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session. Second-ball games add headers to the session total, so count them.

drills.name: Heading Introduction: Kneeling Contact
drills.description: First heading exposure at 13-14. Players kneel on soft grass, facing a partner 2-3 m away. The partner throws the ball underarm to forehead height. The player nods it back to the partner's hands. Kneeling removes jumping and running, so the player can feel the contact point. Each player heads no more than 5 balls.
coaching_points: Contact on the forehead, just below the hairline - not the top of the head
Eyes open, mouth closed, neck firm
Push through the ball with the trunk; do not let the ball hit you

rubric.description: 1 = ball hits face or top of head, eyes shut; 3 = forehead contact on most balls, eyes open, neck firm; 5 = clean forehead contact every ball with the trunk driving through
1 = leans back or flinches as the ball arrives; 3 = moves forward to meet most balls; 5 = meets every ball in front of the body as it arrives
1 = ball rarely reaches the partner; 3 = ball reaches the partner's reach on most balls; 5 = ball lands in the partner's hands every time

drills.progression: Stand and repeat from 2 m (he-007). Stay inside the heading limit for the session.
drills.video_note: Side view at head height showing forehead contact and trunk movement through the ball.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: no heading in training under U12. U12: optional, one session a month, 5 headers per player. U13: optional, one heading session a week at most, 5 headers per player. U14 and older: one heading session a week at most, 10 headers per player per session. In this band keep to 5 headers per player per session unless the player is U14 or older. Heading stays unopposed, with a light, dry ball at low pressure. Never use a wet or over-inflated ball, and do not use a ball that has soaked up water. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session.

drills.name: Heading Introduction: Standing Self-Toss to a Partner
drills.description: Pairs stand 3-4 m apart on soft grass. Each player tosses the ball up gently, heads it to the partner's hands, then swaps. Unopposed, no jumping at first. Cones mark each player's spot. Each player heads no more than 5 balls.
coaching_points: Toss just in front of you and a little above the head
Bend the knees, then drive up and through the ball with legs and trunk
Watch the ball until it touches the forehead
Aim for the partner's hands

rubric.description: 1 = ball hits the face or top of head; 3 = forehead contact on most balls with a firm neck; 5 = clean forehead contact every ball, legs and trunk drive through
1 = heads the ball late or lets it drop; 3 = meets the ball at head height on most balls; 5 = meets every ball at its highest point in front of the body
1 = ball goes wide of the partner; 3 = ball reaches the partner on most balls; 5 = ball reaches the partner's hands every time

drills.progression: Add one step forward into the header, then a two-foot take-off with a lighter toss. Stay inside the limit.
drills.video_note: Side view at head height plus a front view of the partner catching.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: no heading in training under U12. U12: optional, one session a month, 5 headers per player. U13: optional, one heading session a week at most, 5 headers per player. U14 and older: one heading session a week at most, 10 headers per player per session. In this band keep to 5 headers per player per session unless the player is U14 or older. Heading stays unopposed, with a light, dry ball at low pressure. Never use a wet or over-inflated ball, and do not use a ball that has soaked up water. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session.

drills.name: Aerial Timing Game: Jump and Catch (No Heading)
drills.description: Two teams of four on a 20 x 15 m pitch with an end zone at each end. Players throw the ball to a teammate, who jumps and catches it with both hands at the highest point, as if heading it. A catch in the end zone scores. No running with the ball. No head contact. It trains the same timing, flight judgement and take-off as heading, with no load on the head.
coaching_points: Watch the flight of the ball, not the thrower
Take one or two steps and jump off your stronger foot
Catch at the highest point with arms stretched
Land balanced on both feet

rubric.description: 1 = jumps too early or too late on most balls; 3 = catches at or near the highest point on most balls; 5 = catches at the highest point nearly every time
1 = flat-footed or lands off balance; 3 = clean take-off and balanced landing on most jumps; 5 = efficient take-off, arms up, soft balanced landing every time
1 = waits where the ball was thrown; 3 = adjusts feet to the flight on most balls; 5 = reads the flight early and moves to the landing spot before the ball arrives

drills.progression: Add a passive defender who may jump but not touch. Heading work, if any, goes in a separate session inside the weekly limit.
drills.video_note: Wide side view showing run, take-off and landing.
drills.safety_note: No head contact, so this drill adds no headers to a player's count (FA limits: 5 headers per player per session at U13, 10 from U14, one heading session a week at most). Land on both feet. No pushing, climbing or holding opponents. Walk the pitch first and clear holes and stones.

drills.name: Heading to Targets: Short Throws to a Gate
drills.description: Groups of three: a server, a header and a retriever. The server throws underarm from 4-5 m. The header heads the ball through a 2 m cone gate behind the server. Rotate every 2-3 headers. Start with the gate close, then move it back. Unopposed. At 13-14 keep to 5 headers per player; at 15-16 keep to 10.
coaching_points: Head through the ball toward the gate; keep the head still on contact
Step to the ball if it is short; do not stretch your neck for it
Control distance with the trunk, not by snapping the neck

rubric.description: 1 = contact on the face or top of head; 3 = forehead contact and a firm neck on most headers; 5 = clean contact every time with the body behind the ball
1 = fewer than 2 in 5 headers pass through the gate; 3 = 3 in 5 pass through; 5 = 4 or 5 in 5 pass through
1 = quality changes from header to header; 3 = same technique on most headers; 5 = same clean technique on every header, from either side

drills.progression: Move the gate 1 m further each round. At 15-16 use a moving server and lift the cap to 10 headers.
drills.video_note: View from behind the header, showing the gate and the flight of the ball.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: no heading in training under U12. U12: optional, one session a month, 5 headers per player. U13: optional, one heading session a week at most, 5 headers per player. U14 and older: one heading session a week at most, 10 headers per player per session. In this band keep to 5 headers per player per session unless the player is U14 or older. Heading stays unopposed, with a light, dry ball at low pressure. Never use a wet or over-inflated ball, and do not use a ball that has soaked up water. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session.

drills.name: Heading Under Passive Pressure
drills.description: Groups of three: a server, an attacker and a defender. The server throws or passes from 8-10 m. Stage 1: the defender stands beside the attacker and does not jump or touch. Stage 2: the defender may jump but not use hands or arms. The attacker heads toward a target zone or goal. Track every player's header count: 10 maximum per session.
coaching_points: Win the space before the ball arrives: move off the defender
Arms down; do not push or climb
Defender: stay side-on, track the flight and jump at the same time
Attack the ball at its highest point

rubric.description: 1 = stays beside the defender; 3 = gets a step of space on most balls; 5 = wins the space early on nearly every ball
1 = jumps late and is beaten; 3 = meets the ball at the highest point on most balls; 5 = meets it at the highest point almost every time, even under pressure
1 = contact on the face or top of head; 3 = forehead contact and a firm neck on most headers; 5 = clean forehead contact with good direction every time

drills.progression: Move on to he-004 (Aerial Duels) at 17-19, or full contest in match play.
drills.video_note: Side view showing the jump, the space and clean hands.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Keep service short (thrown or passed, under 10 m), not long kicks, and avoid headers after a long run-up. Use a dry ball at low pressure. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session.

drills.name: Defensive Stance & Footwork
drills.description: Shadow defending through a cone pattern: side-on stance, low centre of gravity, small steps, drop steps and recovery turns.
coaching_points: Side-on, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet
Never cross your legs - drop step instead
Eyes on the ball, not the opponent's feet

rubric.description: 1 = stands square on, feet flat, upright; 3 = side-on and low on most reps, feet a little wide; 5 = side-on, low, balanced and ready to move every rep
1 = steps late or lunges at the cone; 3 = moves with the coach's cue on most reps; 5 = moves on the cue every rep and recovers before the next one
1 = turns the wrong way or crosses the feet; 3 = picks the right turn on most reps; 5 = picks the right turn and keeps the attacker on the same side every rep
1 = walks through the pattern; 3 = works at a steady pace for the whole block; 5 = quick, small steps at full effort for the whole block

drills.progression: Add a partner dribbling slowly to shadow, then at full speed.
drills.video_note: Front and side views of the stance; slow-motion drop-step breakdown.

drills.name: 1v1 Defending: Delay, Show Inside/Outside, Tackle Timing
drills.description: Attacker vs defender to goal or end line. Defender works on approach speed, slowing on arrival, dictating direction, and choosing the tackle moment.
coaching_points: Sprint to close, arrive under control
Show the attacker one way - onto their weak foot or the sideline
Tackle when the touch is too big, not before

rubric.description: 1 = stands square and lets the attacker pass on both sides; 3 = side-on on most reps and shows the attacker one way; 5 = side-on, goal-side and steering the attacker to one side every rep
1 = dives in early or stands off too far; 3 = closes fast then slows on arrival on most reps; 5 = closes fast, slows on arrival and tackles only when the touch is loose
1 = tackles at every chance; 3 = waits for a loose touch on most reps; 5 = delays when the tackle is risky and tackles when it will win the ball
1 = jogs and gives up when beaten; 3 = keeps working for the whole block; 5 = full effort and recovers after being beaten, every rep

drills.progression: Add a support attacker so the defender must delay for recovering help.
drills.video_note: Clip series showing approach, dictation, and tackle moment with freeze-frames.

drills.name: Tackling Technique (Block & Poke)
drills.description: Technique block for block tackles (through the ball, big contact surface) and poke tackles (toe through the ball when alongside).
coaching_points: Block tackle: low, firm ankle, drive through the ball
Poke: use the foot nearest the ball only
Stay on your feet - sliding is the last resort

rubric.description: 1 = arrives off balance or from the wrong side; 3 = arrives balanced, with the foot planted, on most reps; 5 = balanced, strong and close to the ball every rep
1 = tackles when the ball is under the attacker's foot; 3 = tackles at or just after the touch on most reps; 5 = tackles as the ball leaves the foot, every rep
1 = picks block or poke at random; 3 = picks the right tackle on most reps; 5 = picks block or poke from the angle and wins the ball cleanly
1 = tackles with no weight behind it; 3 = commits to the ball on most reps; 5 = commits fully with a firm, safe contact every rep

drills.progression: Apply both tackles in a live 1v1 corridor game.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion of each tackle type from the side; contact frames highlighted.

drills.name: Interceptions: Reading the Pass
drills.description: Defender starts between two receivers; server plays to either. Defender reads the passer's shape, anticipates, and intercepts or blocks.
coaching_points: Read the passer's hips and plant foot
Stay goalside but within interception distance
First touch after the intercept goes forward

rubric.description: 1 = stands level with one receiver and cannot reach the other; 3 = stands between both receivers on most reps; 5 = stands on the line between both and moves with the ball every rep
1 = reacts after the pass has left; 3 = starts as the ball leaves on most reps; 5 = starts on the passer's body shape, before the ball leaves
1 = chases the ball after the pass; 3 = cuts the pass off or blocks it on some reps; 5 = reads the pass and wins or blocks the ball on most reps
1 = jogs to the ball; 3 = runs to the ball on most reps; 5 = sprints to the ball and moves on at once, every rep

drills.progression: Add a third receiver and a decision: intercept high or protect the goal.
drills.video_note: Overhead angle showing starting position and the interception lane.

drills.name: Defending in Pairs: Cover & Balance
drills.description: Two defenders vs two attackers with a coach serving. First defender presses, second covers at an angle and distance; roles swap on every pass.
coaching_points: Press and cover - never both square
Cover distance: close enough to intercept the switch
Communicate 'press', 'hold', 'show left/right'

rubric.description: 1 = the cover stands behind the first defender in a line; 3 = the cover is at an angle on most reps; 5 = the cover is at the right angle and distance every rep
1 = both press at once or both wait; 3 = one presses and one covers on most reps; 5 = one presses at the right moment and the other adjusts as the ball moves
1 = roles stay fixed after the pass; 3 = swaps roles after the pass on most reps; 5 = swaps roles at once and says who presses, every rep
1 = walks to the new position; 3 = moves quickly on most reps; 5 = moves at full pace to the new position every rep

drills.progression: Extend to 3v3 with a third defender providing balance on the weak side.

drills.name: Pressing Triggers & Coordinated Press
drills.description: Unit work on pressing triggers (back pass, bad touch, pass to the line) and the coordinated press: who jumps, who screens, who covers behind.
coaching_points: One jumps, everyone shifts - press as a unit
Trigger recognition: back passes and poor first touches
Curve the run to block the return pass

rubric.description: 1 = the group is spread out with gaps between lines; 3 = the group stays compact on most reps; 5 = the group is tight, screens passing lanes and keeps cover behind the presser
1 = presses when nobody is ready; 3 = presses on the trigger on most reps; 5 = all players move on the trigger together, every rep
1 = presses at any time; 3 = knows the triggers and uses them on most reps; 5 = picks the right trigger, and holds the press back when it is not on
1 = presses at jogging pace; 3 = presses hard for most of each burst; 5 = presses at full pace for the whole burst and recovers quickly

drills.progression: Live game where pressing successfully in the final third earns double goals.
drills.video_note: Full-pitch tactical cam with trigger moments freeze-framed and labelled.

drills.name: Recovery Runs & Defending the Space Behind
drills.description: Defender starts goalside-wrong; on the coach's ball in behind, sprints to recover and defend the runner 1v1 before the shot.
coaching_points: Sprint on a line to goal first, then to the ball
Get between ball and goal before engaging
Slow the attacker without diving in

rubric.description: 1 = chases behind the runner; 3 = gets goal-side by the end of the run on most reps; 5 = gets goal-side early and keeps the body between runner and goal
1 = starts after the ball has gone; 3 = starts on the coach's ball on most reps; 5 = starts as the ball is played, every rep
1 = dives in when still behind; 3 = stays on his feet and delays on most reps; 5 = delays until help arrives, then tackles or blocks the shot
1 = jogs back; 3 = sprints for most of the run; 5 = full sprint the whole way, every rep

drills.progression: Two attackers vs one recovering defender - decision under overload.
drills.video_note: Chase-cam angle showing the recovery line and the moment of engagement.

drills.name: Defending the Box: Marking & Clearances
drills.description: Back line plus GK defending repeated crosses: starting positions, zonal vs. man responsibilities, attacking the clearance, and holding the line on the exit.
coaching_points: See ball and man - side-on, arm's contact
Attack the ball for clearances - no free headers
Step out together after the clearance

rubric.description: 1 = stands in the wrong zone or loses the runner; 3 = holds the zone or marks the runner on most crosses; 5 = sees the ball and the runner and holds the right place on every cross
1 = reaches the ball after the attacker; 3 = reaches it first on some crosses; 5 = attacks the ball early and wins the first contact on most crosses
1 = heads or kicks to the middle; 3 = clears wide or high on most reps; 5 = clears wide and high away from goal, every rep
1 = waits for the ball; 3 = challenges on most crosses; 5 = challenges on every cross and is up fast for the next one

drills.progression: Add second-ball attackers and a counter-attack target on the clearance.
drills.video_note: Behind-goal and wide angles; freeze-frames on starting positions.
drills.safety_note: FA youth heading guidance: one heading session a week at most and no more than 10 headers per player per session (U14 to U18). Contested headers may start at U15. Keep service short (thrown or passed, under 10 m), not long kicks, and avoid headers after a long run-up. Use a dry ball at low pressure. Count each player's headers, and add headers from any other drill in the same session. Clearances with the head count toward the limit.

drills.name: Defensive Line Shape (Back Four / Back Three)
drills.description: Unit shadow play: the back line shifts, slides, steps and drops in response to the ball's position, rehearsing distances and communication.
coaching_points: Defend as a connected unit - max gaps between defenders
Ball side steps, far side tucks in
Line leader (usually CB) commands the step and drop

rubric.description: 1 = gaps open between defenders; 3 = the line holds its spacing on most shifts; 5 = the line stays level, compact and one pass from cover, every shift
1 = moves after the ball has moved; 3 = moves with the ball on most shifts; 5 = moves as the ball is played and steps up or drops together
1 = does not know when to step or drop; 3 = steps or drops correctly on most calls; 5 = reads the ball and calls step, drop or hold before it is needed
1 = walks through the shifts; 3 = keeps a steady pace; 5 = moves at match pace and keeps talking, the whole block
