drills.name: Pressure and Cover: 2v2 Basics
drills.description: Two defenders play against two attackers on a 20 x 15 m pitch with a small goal. The first defender pressures the ball with a curved run. The second defender covers 2-3 m behind and to the side, ready to take over. Swap jobs when the ball is passed.
coaching_points: Close down fast, then slow down and get side-on 2 m from the ball
Cover stands behind and to the side, and talks: 'Show him inside!'
Keep the attacker away from goal; do not dive in
Swap jobs when the ball is passed

rubric.description: 1 = both defenders stand side by side; 3 = cover is behind and to the side on most attacks; 5 = cover is in the right spot and adjusts as the ball moves, every time
1 = dives in or approaches too late; 3 = closes down and slows at the right moment on most attacks; 5 = closes and slows at the right moment nearly every time
1 = silent; 3 = cover gives the pressing defender instructions on most attacks; 5 = clear, early calls on every attack

drills.progression: Add a third attacker (3v3). Then see de-005 at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Side view showing the pressure and cover positions.

drills.name: Small-Sided Games (3v3 / 4v4 / 5v5)
drills.description: Free small-sided games on small pitches. High involvement, many decisions, natural repetition of core principles. Coach with guided questions, not constant stoppages.
coaching_points: Let the game teach - intervene with questions
Width and depth in possession, compactness out of it
Rotate players so everyone attacks and defends

rubric.description: 1 = bunches or stands still; 3 = uses width and depth on most possessions and stays compact when the ball is lost; 5 = stays organised in every phase of the game
1 = random choices; 3 = looks for the right option on most possessions; 5 = picks the right option nearly every time
1 = silent; 3 = calls or directs teammates on most possessions; 5 = constant, helpful talk
1 = ball-watches; 3 = scans on most possessions; 5 = scans early and knows the next action before the ball arrives

drills.progression: Add conditions tied to the session theme (e.g., goal counts double after a switch of play).
drills.video_note: Wide fixed angle of a full round; capture goals and key decisions.

drills.name: Positional Games (Juego de Posicion)
drills.description: Zoned positional games (e.g., 4v4+3) where players must occupy their zones. Trains positioning, angles, and playing through lines per your game model.
coaching_points: Occupy your zone - trust the structure
Play between lines, receive side-on
Support behind, beside, and beyond the ball

rubric.description: 1 = leaves the zone or bunches; 3 = holds the zone and gives passing lines most of the time; 5 = holds the structure and supports behind, beside and beyond the ball
1 = plays into pressure; 3 = plays between the lines on most possessions; 5 = finds the line-breaking pass nearly every time
1 = receives facing the ball; 3 = receives side-on on most passes; 5 = receives side-on and sees the game every time
1 = silent; 3 = calls on most possessions; 5 = tells teammates where the space is

drills.progression: Add a counter-pressing rule on loss and transition targets at the edges.
drills.video_note: Overhead angle with zone lines visible; freeze on line-breaking passes.

drills.name: Phases of Play: Build-Up, Progression, Final Third
drills.description: Coached walk-through to game-speed rehearsal of one phase at a time: building from the GK, progressing through midfield, and final-third combinations.
coaching_points: Start positions must match your match-day shape
Every pass has a pre-planned next action
Recognise when to break the pattern and improvise

rubric.description: 1 = starts out of shape; 3 = starts in the match-day shape on most reps; 5 = right shape at every phase and re-sets quickly
1 = no planned next action; 3 = knows the next action on most possessions; 5 = knows it and breaks the pattern at the right time
1 = misses the cues; 3 = reads the trigger on most possessions; 5 = reads the cue early nearly every time
1 = silent; 3 = calls the pattern on most possessions; 5 = the whole unit talks in step

drills.progression: Chain all three phases into one continuous attack against a live defence.
drills.video_note: Full-pitch tactical cam per phase with freeze-frames on rotation triggers.

drills.name: Transition Games (5-Second Rule)
drills.description: Possession game with a hard transition rule: on loss, counter-press for 5 seconds; on regain, play forward within 5 seconds. Goals scored in transition count double.
coaching_points: Nearest player presses the ball instantly
On regain: first look forward
Rest defence stays connected while attacking

rubric.description: 1 = no clear reaction on a loss or a regain; 3 = presses or plays forward on most turnovers; 5 = picks the right reaction nearly every turnover
1 = rest defence is not in place; 3 = rest defence is connected on most attacks; 5 = rest defence is set every time
1 = slow to react; 3 = counter-press starts within a second on most turnovers; 5 = counter-press starts at once nearly every turnover
1 = silent; 3 = calls press and cover on most turnovers; 5 = clear calls from the whole group

drills.progression: Vary the rule by phase: 3-second counter-press for older groups.
drills.video_note: Wide angle capturing the moment of turnover and both teams' reactions.

drills.name: Conditioned Overload Games (4v2, 5v3 to Goal)
drills.description: Attack vs defence with deliberate overloads. Attackers learn patience and width; defenders learn to delay, screen, and protect the centre.
coaching_points: Attack: move the ball fast to stretch the block
Defence: protect the middle, show wide
Finish the attack quickly when the gap opens

rubric.description: 1 = attackers bunch and defenders stand flat; 3 = attackers stretch the block on most possessions and defenders protect the middle; 5 = every attack stretches the block and every defence protects the centre
1 = rushes or stalls; 3 = patient on most possessions; 5 = matches patience and speed to the gap
1 = misses the moment the gap opens; 3 = finishes quickly when the gap opens, on most possessions; 5 = takes nearly every gap
1 = silent; 3 = calls for the ball or gives instructions on most possessions; 5 = clear, constant talk

drills.progression: Flip the overload (underload attack) to train individual superiority and combination quality.
drills.video_note: Tactical wide angle; annotate the moment the overload creates the free player.

drills.name: Team Video Analysis Session
drills.description: Guided team review of short clips (30-60s) tied to the current training theme. Players answer: what do you see, what are the options, what was the best choice?
coaching_points: One theme per session - don't review everything
Ask players before telling them
Link every clip back to a training drill

rubric.description: 1 = watches without joining in; 3 = answers when asked and joins the discussion; 5 = leads discussion points and asks questions
1 = says what happened only; 3 = names options and gives reasons; 5 = compares options and says what was best and why
1 = no link to the session; 3 = links most clips to the theme; 5 = links every clip to a drill and says what to change

drills.progression: Assign players to present a clip themselves - ownership accelerates learning.
drills.video_note: Example annotated clip with telestration (arrows, zones, player tracks).

drills.name: Individual Tactical Video Review
drills.description: Player watches 5-10 of their own clips (good and bad decisions) with coach annotations and leaves written or voice-note reflections. Pairs directly with the self-feedback feature.
coaching_points: Review decisions, not just highlights
Pause before each key moment: what were the options?
Finish with one concrete focus for the next session

rubric.description: 1 = watches a few clips and adds no notes; 3 = watches all clips and adds notes; 5 = watches all clips twice and adds clear notes on each
1 = no change in matches; 3 = tries one idea in training; 5 = tries the ideas in training and in matches
1 = says only 'good' or 'bad'; 3 = names the good and bad choices; 5 = names the choice, the better option and what to look for next time

drills.progression: Player tags and annotates their own clips before the coach reviews them.
drills.video_note: Example of an annotated individual clip with coach voice-over.

drills.name: Playing Out from the Back: 4v3 Build-Up
drills.description: Mark a 40 x 30 m area with a build-up zone at one end (15 m) and a midfield zone beyond it. In the build-up zone a keeper and three defenders play against three forwards. One midfielder waits in the next zone. The team scores by passing out of the build-up zone to the midfielder, who turns and passes to a target at the far end line. Forwards may not enter the midfield zone.
coaching_points: Spread wide to make angles, then pass and move
The keeper is the extra player
Play past the first presser, not into him
Look over your shoulder before the ball arrives

rubric.description: 1 = players bunch together and block each other's passes; 3 = clear angles and width on most possessions; 5 = shape gives easy passing lanes on every possession
1 = forces passes into pressure; 3 = finds the free player on most possessions; 5 = picks the safest forward pass nearly every time
1 = receives without looking; 3 = checks over the shoulder before most passes; 5 = scans early and knows the next pass before the ball arrives

drills.progression: Add a fourth forward, then play the same build-up in a full game.
drills.video_note: Raised wide view of the whole area showing angles and spacing.

drills.name: Width and Depth: 4v4 with Wide Targets
drills.description: Play 4v4 on a 30 x 25 m pitch with a neutral wide player on each touchline (one touch only). A team scores by playing through a wide target and then to a teammate who dribbles or receives in the end zone. A team must use a wide player before it can score.
coaching_points: Spread out when you have the ball and close up when you lose it
Offer on different lines: one short, one long
Use the wide player to open the game, then look for the space inside
Move after you pass

rubric.description: 1 = players stand in the same line or bunch; 3 = uses width and depth on most possessions; 5 = clear width and depth with passing lanes on every possession
1 = always plays the first pass or the same side; 3 = uses the wide player when it helps on most possessions; 5 = switches play at the right moment nearly every time
1 = silent; 3 = calls for the ball and gives short instructions on most possessions; 5 = talks constantly and clearly to link play

drills.progression: Remove the one-touch limit for targets and add a fifth attacker.
drills.video_note: Raised wide view showing team shape as the ball moves.

drills.name: Scan and Switch: 3v3 + 1 Neutral Possession
drills.description: Play 3v3 plus one neutral player in a 20 x 20 m grid. The team with the ball scores a point for eight passes in a row. The neutral always plays for the team that has the ball. The coach freezes play at random and asks the player on the ball: 'Who was free?' A right answer scores a bonus point.
coaching_points: Look before the ball arrives: check your shoulders
Receive on the side away from pressure
Pass and move to a new passing lane

rubric.description: 1 = never looks before receiving; 3 = checks over the shoulder before most passes; 5 = scans early and names the free teammate when asked
1 = passes to the nearest player; 3 = finds the free player on most passes; 5 = finds the free player nearly every time
1 = passes often lost; 3 = passes reach a teammate on most attempts; 5 = accurate, well weighted passes nearly every time

drills.progression: Add a second neutral, or limit play to two touches.
drills.video_note: Raised wide view of the grid; freeze the game at the 'Who was free?' moment.

drills.name: Lose It, Win It: First Five Seconds After Losing the Ball
drills.description: Play 4v4 on a 30 x 25 m pitch with a small goal at each end. When a team loses the ball it has five seconds to win it back as a group. If it cannot, all four players run back past the ball into their own half. Count the five seconds aloud. A goal scored within eight seconds of winning the ball counts double.
coaching_points: The nearest player presses at once; the others close the passing lanes
If you cannot win it in five seconds, drop back and protect your goal
Talk: call who presses and who covers
After winning it, play forward quickly

rubric.description: 1 = chases the ball alone or stands still after losing it; 3 = presses or drops back sensibly on most turnovers; 5 = picks press or drop correctly nearly every time
1 = nobody covers the presser; 3 = a cover player is in place on most presses; 5 = the group presses as a unit on every turnover
1 = silent; 3 = calls 'press' or 'drop' on most turnovers; 5 = clear calls from the whole group on every turnover
1 = slow to react after losing it; 3 = reacts within a second on most turnovers; 5 = reacts at once on nearly every turnover

drills.progression: Increase to 5v5 on a larger pitch. See ta-004 at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Raised wide view; replay the first five seconds after a turnover.
drills.safety_note: High intensity. Give a water break every 8-10 minutes, more often in hot weather.

drills.name: Catching Foundations (W-Shape, Scoop, High Ball)
drills.description: Core handling block: W-shape for head-height balls, diamond/scoop for low balls, and secure high-ball catching. Served at controlled pace, building speed.
coaching_points: Set position before every serve
Hands first, body behind the ball as insurance
Soft elbows - cushion the catch into the body

rubric.description: 1 = hands wide or palms flat, ball bounces off the chest; 3 = hands behind the ball and a soft catch on most balls; 5 = clean W or scoop shape, ball held safely every time
1 = stands on the line or too far to one side; 3 = gets in line with the ball on most shots; 5 = sets in line with the ball and balanced before every serve
1 = catches when a block is safer; 3 = picks catch or parry sensibly on most balls; 5 = picks the safe option every time and holds the ball
1 = silent; 3 = calls 'keeper' on most high balls; 5 = calls loud and early on every high ball

drills.progression: Randomise serve height and add footwork before each catch.
drills.video_note: Front close-up of hand shapes plus full-body view of the set position.

drills.name: Diving Technique (Collapse, Low, Full Extension)
drills.description: Progressive diving block: collapse dive from kneeling, low dive from standing, then full extension. Both sides equally.
coaching_points: First step toward the ball, hands lead
Land on the side, not the stomach or elbows
Attack the ball - don't wait for it

rubric.description: 1 = falls flat or lands on the elbow; 3 = pushes off and lands on the side of the body on most dives; 5 = pushes off and lands on the side with the hands leading, both sides
1 = starts off balance or square; 3 = starts set and ready on most reps; 5 = starts set and balanced in the right place every rep
1 = dives when the ball is within reach; 3 = dives only when needed on most reps; 5 = dives only when needed and picks the right type of dive
1 = silent; 3 = calls the next serve on most reps; 5 = calls and resets quickly after every dive

drills.progression: Add a deflection or a second-ball reaction after the save.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion side view of each dive type with the first-step highlighted.

drills.name: Shot-Stopping from Angles & Near-Post Positioning
drills.description: Shots from wide and central angles at varied distances. Focus on angle play, near-post coverage, and set timing relative to the strike.
coaching_points: Narrow the angle - come off the line as the shooter approaches
Set as the striker's foot contacts the ball
Near post is yours: no goals beaten there

rubric.description: 1 = set late, moving at the strike; 3 = set at the strike on most shots; 5 = set at the strike with hands ready, every shot
1 = leaves the near post open; 3 = covers the near post on most shots; 5 = covers the near post and the angle on every shot
1 = pushes the ball back into the danger area; 3 = catches or parries to a safe side on most shots; 5 = holds the ball, or parries wide, every time
1 = silent; 3 = talks to the wall or defenders on most shots; 5 = organises the wall and defenders before every shot

drills.progression: Add a cutback option so the GK must reposition across goal mid-attack.
drills.video_note: Behind-goal angle showing starting position and movement line.

drills.name: Reactions & Reflex Saves
drills.description: Close-range rapid-fire serves, deflections off a board or mannequin, and seated/lying starts. Trains explosive reactions and recovery.
coaching_points: Stay big - don't shrink at close range
Recover to set immediately after each save
Hands up in the ready position at all times

rubric.description: 1 = hands late and the ball goes through; 3 = hands reach the ball on most serves; 5 = quick hands and a firm wrist on nearly every serve
1 = starts flat-footed; 3 = starts on the balls of the feet on most reps; 5 = starts balanced and ready after every recovery
1 = tries to catch every fast ball; 3 = parries when a catch is unsafe on most reps; 5 = catches when safe, parries wide when not, every rep
1 = no reset after a save; 3 = resets and gets ready on most reps; 5 = gets up fast and calls 'ready' every time

drills.progression: Random two-server setup: GK must find the ball being served.
drills.video_note: Rapid-fire clip showing 5-6 consecutive saves and recoveries.

drills.name: Dealing with Crosses (Catch, Punch, Claim Through Traffic)
drills.description: Crosses delivered from both flanks with increasing traffic. GK decides catch vs. punch, attacks the ball at the highest point, and commands the box.
coaching_points: Start deep enough to attack the ball forward
Call early and loud: 'KEEPER' or 'AWAY'
Punch high, wide, and far when you can't catch

rubric.description: 1 = jumps off two feet or reaches late; 3 = jumps off one foot and reaches the ball on most crosses; 5 = strong one-foot jump, high contact point, ball held or punched clear
1 = starts on the line; 3 = starts off the line on most crosses; 5 = starts in a place where all cross types can be reached
1 = comes for balls he cannot reach; 3 = picks come or stay sensibly on most crosses; 5 = comes only for balls he can win and stays for the rest
1 = silent in traffic; 3 = calls 'keeper' on most crosses; 5 = loud and early on every cross, defenders know who has it

drills.progression: Live attackers contesting and a second-ball rule on spills.
drills.video_note: Behind-goal angle showing the attack line to the ball and the call timing.

drills.name: 1v1 Situations (Closing Down, Spreading, Smothering)
drills.description: Through-balls and dribbles at the GK. Decision framework: stay, spread (star jump), block, or smother, based on touch quality and angle.
coaching_points: Sprint to close while the touch is loose
Spread big and low on the striker's touch
Smother when the ball is free - hands first, brave

rubric.description: 1 = falls over or leaves a gap under the body; 3 = spreads or blocks with a firm body shape on most reps; 5 = big, balanced shape with hands and feet behind the ball every rep
1 = comes out late or stays on the line; 3 = comes off the line at a good angle on most reps; 5 = closes the angle fast and stops at the right moment
1 = dives early and is beaten; 3 = stays up until the touch is loose on most reps; 5 = stays up, reads the touch, and picks smother, spread or block
1 = silent; 3 = calls on some reps; 5 = calls and signals to defenders on every rep

drills.progression: Add a second attacker so the GK must also cover the square pass.
drills.video_note: Striker-cam and behind-goal angles; freeze on the decision moment.

drills.name: Throwing Distribution (Roll, Javelin, Overarm)
drills.description: Distribution accuracy block: roll-outs to fullbacks, javelin/sidearm throws to midfielders, and overarm throws to wide targets, all into marked zones.
coaching_points: Roll: low, firm, into the receiver's path
Javelin: side-on, sling from the hip for distance
Hit moving targets in stride, not to feet

rubric.description: 1 = throw wobbles or lands short; 3 = clean throw to the target on most reps; 5 = flat, firm, accurate throws to each target type
1 = throws to a marked player; 3 = picks the free player on most reps; 5 = picks the free player and the right throw every rep
1 = less than half reach the zone; 3 = about two in three reach the zone; 5 = nine in ten reach the zone with a good pace

drills.progression: Add a time pressure: distribute within 3 seconds of catching.
drills.video_note: Side view of each technique plus a wide shot of zone accuracy.

drills.name: Kicking Distribution (Goal Kicks, Side Volleys, Drop Kicks)
drills.description: Full kicking block: goal kicks to wide zones, driven side volleys to midfield targets, and drop kicks for distance. Accuracy scored per zone.
coaching_points: Body shape matches the intended flight
Strike through the bottom half for loft, middle for driven
Scan before receiving - distribution starts before the catch

rubric.description: 1 = mis-hits or slices the ball; 3 = clean contact on most kicks; 5 = clean contact with a good follow-through, both goal kicks and volleys
1 = kicks long every time; 3 = picks the zone on most kicks; 5 = picks the zone from the game: short, mid or long
1 = less than half reach the zone; 3 = about two in three reach the zone; 5 = nine in ten reach the zone at the right height

drills.progression: Distribute to moving targets making timed runs into zones.
drills.video_note: Wide view of ball flight to zones; slow-motion contact insert.

drills.name: Playing Out from the Back (GK + Defenders)
drills.description: GK as the first attacker: building with centre-backs split, pivot drops, and fullbacks high, against a passive then active first line of pressure.
coaching_points: GK comfortable on both feet - receive side-on
Defenders open body shape to play forward
Recognise the press: bounce, switch, or go over it

rubric.description: 1 = heavy first touch or weak pass; 3 = controlled touch and a firm pass on most reps; 5 = one or two clean touches and an accurate pass with both feet
1 = stays on the line; 3 = offers an angle for the pass on most reps; 5 = moves to give a clear passing line for each defender
1 = plays into pressure; 3 = picks the free player on most reps; 5 = picks the free player and plays long only when short is blocked
1 = silent; 3 = talks to defenders on most reps; 5 = tells the defenders where to go before the pass

drills.progression: Live pressing front three; conceding or losing the ball has consequences.
drills.video_note: Tactical wide angle with the pressing shape and passing lanes highlighted.

drills.name: Sweeper-Keeper: Through Balls & Playing Behind the Line
drills.description: Balls played in behind a high line. GK reads the flight early, sprints to clear or receive outside the box, and redistributes or protects.
coaching_points: Starting position: high enough to sweep, deep enough to recover
Decide early: commit fully or hold the box
Communicate with the line on every ball in behind

rubric.description: 1 = mis-kicks or loses balance when clearing; 3 = clears or controls under little pressure on most reps; 5 = clean clearance or control outside the box every rep
1 = stays on the line; 3 = starts a few metres off the line on most reps; 5 = starts at the right height for the defence and moves with the ball
1 = comes out for balls he cannot reach; 3 = picks go or stay sensibly on most reps; 5 = picks go early and stays when the runner is first, every rep
1 = silent; 3 = calls on most reps; 5 = tells the line to step or drop before the ball is played

drills.progression: Live striker timing runs against a real defensive line with offsides active.
drills.video_note: Tactical cam showing starting position, the trigger ball, and the clearance.

drills.name: Organising the Defence & Set-Piece Command
drills.description: Walk-through to live set pieces and open play where the GK's communication is the measured skill: marking assignments, line height, and early warnings.
coaching_points: Talk early - before the ball is played, not after
Short, specific commands with names
Own the six-yard box on every delivery

rubric.description: 1 = calls late, or only after the ball is played; 3 = early, clear calls on most set pieces; 5 = early, short, named commands every time, and the defence moves on them
1 = reacts after the ball is played; 3 = warns of danger early on most set pieces; 5 = warns early and reads the delivery before it is struck
1 = line height and marking are wrong or unclear; 3 = sets marking and line height on most set pieces; 5 = sets the line and the marking before every delivery
1 = claims or stays at random; 3 = calls claim or stay correctly on most deliveries; 5 = owns the six-yard box and picks right nearly every delivery

drills.progression: Score the defensive unit's organisation on set pieces with the GK as the conductor.
drills.video_note: Clip with audio: GK's calls audible before and during set pieces.

drills.name: Ready Stance and Footwork: Set, Shuffle, Recover
drills.description: Mark a line 4 m wide with cones. The keeper starts in the ready stance: feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, hands up in front. The keeper shuffles from cone to cone without crossing the feet, stops and sets on each cone, and makes a save when the coach or a partner rolls or throws a ball. Add a drop step backward, then a recovery to the centre.
coaching_points: Set (stop) before the ball is hit; a keeper who is moving cannot react
Feet never cross or click together
Hands up in front with the palms to the ball
Head still, eyes on the ball

rubric.description: 1 = upright stance, feet cross or click; 3 = balanced stance and clean side-steps on most reps; 5 = low balanced stance, light feet and hands ready on every rep
1 = still moving when the ball is played; 3 = sets before the ball on most reps; 5 = sets before the ball on nearly every rep and reacts at once
1 = ends off line or off centre; 3 = recovers to a sensible central position on most reps; 5 = recovers to the best position quickly on every rep

drills.progression: The coach calls left, right or back at random. Finish each shuffle with a save.
drills.video_note: Front view of the stance and a side view of the footwork.
drills.safety_note: Walk the area first and clear stones and holes.

drills.name: Saves and Rebounds: Push Wide, Not Into Danger
drills.description: A shooter strikes from 12-16 m at moderate power, along the ground and at waist height. The keeper catches the ball if it is safe to hold. If not, the keeper pushes it wide of goal and away from the middle, never back into the penalty area. The shooter follows up to test the rebound. The keeper gets back to the set position after every save.
coaching_points: Catch when you can hold it; push away only when you cannot
Get your body behind the ball as a second barrier
Push the ball wide of goal, away from the centre
Get up and set at once; the second shot is where goals come from

rubric.description: 1 = hands late or soft, ball squirms away; 3 = body behind the ball and firm hands on most saves; 5 = firm hands and a sound body shape on every save
1 = pushes the ball back into the middle or holds when it is unsafe; 3 = chooses well on most shots; 5 = catches when safe and pushes wide when not, nearly every time
1 = slow to get up after a save; 3 = set again before the follow-up on most saves; 5 = set again before the follow-up every time

drills.progression: Shoot from different angles and add a second shooter for the rebound.
drills.video_note: View from behind the goal showing the push and the recovery.
drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar. Dive only on grass or soft ground. Walk the area first and clear stones, glass and holes. On hard, dry ground keep to kneeling and crouching saves.

drills.name: Narrowing the Angle: Cones and String
drills.description: Run string from each post to a cone on the ball. The string shows the shooting angle. The keeper steps out along the line from the ball to the middle of the goal until the gaps on each side are as small as they can be without being chipped. Move the ball to new spots. Then remove the string and let the shooter strike.
coaching_points: Start on the line between the ball and the middle of the goal
Come out as the ball comes closer, then set
Take small steps and be set when the ball is struck
Do not go so far out that a chip beats you

rubric.description: 1 = stays on the goal line or goes out off line; 3 = on the line to the middle of goal on most shots; 5 = on the best line and distance for every ball position
1 = still moving as the shot is struck; 3 = set as the ball is struck on most shots; 5 = set as the ball is struck on nearly every shot
1 = comes out or stays back with no reason; 3 = judges well on most shots; 5 = reads the shooter and picks the right distance every time

drills.progression: Remove the string and let the shooter dribble in. Then play 1v1 (gk-006).
drills.video_note: View from behind the keeper, showing the string and the keeper's line.
drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar. Keep string low and visible, and take it away before shooting starts.

drills.name: High Balls Introduction: Catch at the Highest Point
drills.description: A server crosses or throws the ball from the wing, 8-15 m out, with no attackers in the area. The keeper starts on the goal line, calls 'Keeper!', takes off from one foot with the knee raised, catches at the highest point with both hands and lands balanced. Build from throws to soft kicks.
coaching_points: Call early and loudly: 'Keeper!'
Take off from one foot and drive the knee up
Catch at the highest point with both hands behind the ball
Land balanced and hold the ball to your chest

rubric.description: 1 = silent or calls late; 3 = calls loud and early on most balls; 5 = calls clearly and early on every ball
1 = flat-footed, catches against the body, lands off balance; 3 = one-foot take-off and a secure catch on most balls; 5 = strong take-off, knee up, secure catch and balanced landing every time
1 = catches the ball on the way down; 3 = catches at or near the highest point on most balls; 5 = catches at the highest point nearly every time

drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar. No contact in this drill. Walk the area first and clear stones and holes.

drills.name: Back-Pass Law: Control and Pass with the Feet
drills.description: A defender passes back along the ground to the keeper. A keeper may not handle a ball a teammate kicks to them on purpose (Law 12), so the keeper controls it with the feet and passes to a target: a wide teammate or through a cone gate. Add a presser who starts 10 m away. Then add a first-time clearance with the instep.

First touch away from pressure, with either foot
Pass or clear with the next touch; do not dwell on it
Hands stay down; never pick it up

1 = never looks before the ball arrives; 3 = checks over the shoulder on most balls; 5 = checks early and knows where the pressure is on every ball
1 = holds on too long or clears without need; 3 = chooses pass or clear well on most balls; 5 = chooses correctly under pressure nearly every time

drills.progression: Add a second presser, then play two-touch, then play from a goal kick into the build-up (sp-012).
drills.video_note: Wide view of the keeper's first touch and the pass.

drills.name: Attacking Corner Routines
drills.description: Rehearse 2-3 corner routines: near-post flick, far-post overload, and short corner. Timed runs, blockers/screens, and delivery targets.

Every routine has a second-ball plan

1 = runs arrive early or late; 3 = runs are timed to the taker's trigger on most corners; 5 = every run is timed
1 = delivery misses the target zone; 3 = delivery reaches the zone on most corners; 5 = right height, pace and zone every corner
1 = blockers and runners overlap; 3 = blockers make space on most corners; 5 = blockers make legal space and there is a second-ball plan, every corner

drills.progression: Run routines against a live zonal defence; score them like a match.
drills.video_note: Overhead diagram of each routine plus live execution clips.

drills.name: Wide Free Kicks: Delivery & Timed Runs
drills.description: Deliveries from wide free-kick positions: inswing, outswing, and driven balls, with coordinated runs attacking corridors between GK and defence.
coaching_points: Delivery: hit the corridor of uncertainty
Attackers attack different zones - front, central, back
One runner stays for the edge-of-box second ball

1 = runners arrive early or late; 3 = most runners arrive with the ball; 5 = all runners arrive with the ball

drills.progression: Live defensive line with GK; track conversion rate per delivery type.
drills.video_note: Wide angle showing the delivery arc and the run corridors.

drills.name: Direct Free-Kick Technique (Over & Around the Wall)
drills.description: Individual repetition block: whip over the wall and curl around it from 18-28m. Log strike location and outcome for trend tracking.
coaching_points: Consistent run-up and plant position every time
Whip: strike low-inside, snap over the ball
Around: outside-foot curl or inside-foot bend - pick your side

rubric.description: 1 = different run-up every time, poor contact; 3 = repeatable run-up and clean contact on most kicks; 5 = same run-up, plant and contact every kick, over or around the wall as chosen
1 = ball flight is unpredictable; 3 = repeats the same shape on most kicks; 5 = same strike shape and target every kick
1 = fewer than 2 of 10 on target; 3 = 4 or 5 of 10 on target; 5 = 6 or more of 10 on target and at least 2 scored

drills.progression: Add a live jumping wall and a GK; keep a personal conversion log.
drills.video_note: Slow-motion contact frames for both techniques plus a goal-cam of the flight.

drills.name: Direct Free-Kick Routines
drills.description: Multi-player free-kick routines: layoff-and-strike, decoy runners, and short passes to change the angle. Rehearsed at game speed.
coaching_points: Decoy runs must be believable
Layoff weight: perfect for the striker's first-time hit
Everyone knows the signal for each routine

rubric.description: 1 = no signals; 3 = signal is known on most routines; 5 = everyone knows the signal and their job
1 = layoff weight is poor; 3 = layoff weight is good on most reps; 5 = perfect weight for a first-time strike nearly every rep
1 = same routine every time; 3 = picks the routine from the wall set-up on most kicks; 5 = reads the wall and picks the best option every kick
1 = decoys are obvious; 3 = decoy runs are believable on most reps; 5 = decoys and runner time together every rep

drills.progression: Opposing wall and GK live; choose the routine based on the wall setup.
drills.video_note: Overhead diagram per routine plus live clips.

drills.name: Throw-In Routines
drills.description: Structured throw-ins in all thirds: creating the free receiver, long throws into the box (if a specialist), and safe retention patterns in your own third.
coaching_points: Move before the thrower picks the ball up
Check away then come short - create two options
Defensive third: retention first, always

rubric.description: 1 = stands still; 3 = creates a free receiver on most throws; 5 = gives two options every throw
1 = takes the throw without looking; 3 = checks for free players on most throws; 5 = picks the best option fast, in every third
1 = silent; 3 = calls for the ball on most throws; 5 = signals the routine early
1 = risky throws in the own third; 3 = safe options in the own third on most throws; 5 = keeps the ball in the own third and takes the chance in the final third, every time

drills.progression: Live marking; score by whether possession is retained 10 seconds after the throw.
drills.video_note: Overhead diagram of movements plus live examples in each third.

drills.name: Penalty Technique & Pre-Shot Routine
drills.description: Repeatable penalty process: consistent run-up, placement over power, a decided target, and a personal pre-shot breathing routine. Log outcomes per corner.
coaching_points: Decide the corner before the run-up - and commit
Breathe, visualise, execute: same routine every time
Placement beats power under pressure

rubric.description: 1 = unbalanced, poor contact; 3 = clean strike with a consistent run-up on most kicks; 5 = clean, accurate and balanced every time
1 = no routine; 3 = same routine on most kicks; 5 = same routine on every kick, including after a miss
1 = changes mind during the run-up; 3 = picks the corner first and commits on most kicks; 5 = picks and commits every time, even under pressure

drills.progression: Simulate match pressure: score or run, crowd noise, or end-of-session deciders.
drills.video_note: Goal-cam of technique plus a walkthrough of the pre-shot routine.

drills.name: Defensive Corners (Zonal, Man, Hybrid)
drills.description: Set up and rehearse your defensive corner system: zonal line on the six-yard box, man-marking assignments, or a hybrid. Includes roles for the edge and counter-attack outlets.
coaching_points: Zonal defenders attack the ball in their zone
Man markers: goalside, ball-side, physical
Two players positioned for the counter on clearance

rubric.description: 1 = loses the opponent or leaves the zone empty; 3 = holds the mark or zone on most corners; 5 = holds the job every corner and the counter-attack outlets are set
1 = attacks the ball late or too early; 3 = attacks the ball in the zone on most corners; 5 = wins first contact on most deliveries
1 = switches between mark and zone for no reason; 3 = keeps to the agreed system on most corners; 5 = adjusts to the routine in time and the outlets leave at the right moment
1 = passive in the contest; 3 = physical and committed on most corners; 5 = wins first contact and the second ball, with legal strength

drills.progression: Defend live attacking routines; review on video and track first-contact win rate.
drills.video_note: Behind-goal and wide angles with each player's zone/assignment annotated.

drills.name: Defensive Free Kicks: Wall Setup & GK Positioning
drills.description: Wall construction by distance and angle: wall size, who anchors it, jump/no-jump calls, and GK positioning behind the wall's protection.
coaching_points: Wall sizes by zone: pre-agreed numbers
Anchor sets the wall on the near-post line
GK positions to own the far half of the goal

rubric.description: 1 = wall stands in the wrong place or leaves a gap; 3 = wall lines up on the post-side of the ball on most kicks; 5 = wall is the right size, in the right place and set quickly, every kick
1 = wall jumps early or late; 3 = wall jumps together on most kicks; 5 = wall jumps on the call and stays up until the ball is past
1 = wall size and jump call do not fit the distance; 3 = picks a sensible size and call on most kicks; 5 = picks the size and jump call from the distance and angle every time
1 = wall drifts and the players talk over each other; 3 = wall holds on most kicks; 5 = wall holds firm, loud calls, every kick

drills.progression: Live takers with routine options; the unit must reset quickly between reps.
drills.video_note: Overhead diagram of wall geometry plus GK-eye-view positioning clip.

drills.name: Throw-In Technique and Quick Restarts
drills.description: Pairs practise a legal throw-in on the touchline: both feet on or behind the line and on the ground, facing the field, ball from behind the head with both hands. The receiver moves to give a short option along the ground. Then play a live 4v4 where every restart is a throw-in. A quick restart that keeps possession for three passes scores a point.
coaching_points: Keep both feet on the ground until the ball is gone
Use both hands; the ball goes back behind the head and over it
Receiver: check away, then come back to feet
Throw to feet or into space the receiver can run onto

rubric.description: 1 = illegal throw (lifts a foot, one hand or no swing behind the head); 3 = legal throw on most attempts; 5 = legal, balanced and repeatable every time
1 = throw rarely reaches a teammate; 3 = throw reaches feet or space on most attempts; 5 = accurate, well weighted throw every time
1 = takes the throw without looking; 3 = checks for a free player on most throws; 5 = picks the best option quickly, and receivers move before the throw

drills.progression: Throw down the line to a wide player, then to a player running onto it. Continue with sp-005 (routines).
drills.video_note: Front and side view of the throwing action, and a wide view of the receivers' movement.
drills.safety_note: Warm up shoulders and back first. Keep the throw smooth, with no big stretch from the back.

drills.name: Attacking Corners: Short Corner and Low Cut-Back
drills.description: Practise two simple routines against four defenders and a keeper. Routine 1, short corner: the taker plays short to a teammate who returns the ball or passes into the area. Routine 2, low cut-back: the taker drives a low ball to the penalty spot for a run-on finish with the foot. There is no heading in this drill, so it stays inside the FA heading limits for this age.
coaching_points: Agree the signal before the corner is taken
Runners start 8-10 m away and arrive as the ball does
Deliver low, firm and away from the keeper
Shoot first time and follow the rebound

rubric.description: 1 = no signal, players unsure of the routine; 3 = signal is clear and used on most corners; 5 = clear signal and everyone knows their job every time
1 = runners arrive early or late; 3 = runners arrive with the ball on most corners; 5 = runs arrive with the ball nearly every time
1 = delivery misses the target zone; 3 = delivery reaches the zone on most corners; 5 = low, firm delivery to the zone every time

drills.progression: Add a third routine, a ball to the far post for a foot finish. See sp-001 at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Overhead or raised view of the movement, plus a close view of the delivery.
drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar.

drills.name: Free Kicks: Quick Restart or Set Piece?
drills.description: Play a 6v6 game. The coach blows for fouls. The team with the free kick chooses: take it quickly before the defence sets, or wait and set a pass or a shot. Defenders must stand 9.15 m (10 yards) from the ball. A restart that leads to a shot or a pass beyond two defenders scores a point.
coaching_points: Look first: is the defence set? If not, play at once
Quick restarts: pass to feet and keep the ball on the ground
Set pieces: one player strikes and one stays back against a counter
Defenders: go back 9.15 m, do not stand over the ball

rubric.description: 1 = always takes it quickly or always waits; 3 = picks the right choice on most free kicks; 5 = reads the defence and picks the best choice nearly every time
1 = free kick loses possession on most attempts; 3 = free kick keeps possession on most attempts; 5 = free kick creates a chance or gains ground nearly every time
1 = does not check where defenders are; 3 = checks the defence on most free kicks; 5 = scans before every free kick and team-mates move to help

drills.progression: Add a wall of three for the defending team and a shot option for players who can strike. See sp-003 at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Wide view showing the restart decision and the defenders' retreat.

drills.name: Goal Kicks: Play Out Under Today's Laws
drills.description: A keeper, two centre backs, two full backs and one holding midfielder play against two pressers. Under the current Laws the ball is in play once it is kicked and clearly moves. Opponents wait outside the penalty area until then, and a teammate may receive it inside the area. The keeper plays short to a defender, or long to a target when the press is high. Score by reaching the halfway line with control.
coaching_points: Decide before the kick: short or long?
Wide players show on both sides to give an angle
Pass away from the pressers, toward the side with space
If the press is on, play long past it; do not force it

rubric.description: 1 = plays short into pressure every time; 3 = reads the press and chooses well on most kicks; 5 = picks the right short or long option nearly every time
1 = players bunch together or stand in the pressers' lines; 3 = good shape and angles on most kicks; 5 = clear angles and wide options on every kick
1 = most passes are loose or lost; 3 = most passes reach a teammate under pressure; 5 = accurate, well weighted passes under pressure nearly every time

drills.progression: Add a third presser, then run the same shape in a full game. See gk-009 at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Wide raised view showing the shape and the pressers' positions.
drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar.

drills.name: Defending Corners: Know Your Opponent and Your Zone
drills.description: Five defenders and a keeper defend against five attackers and a taker. Each defender has one job: mark a named opponent, or hold a zone (near post, penalty spot, far post). The keeper calls and claims. Clear with the foot first; no heading practice here, to stay inside FA heading limits at this age.
coaching_points: Know your job before the corner is taken and say it out loud
Stay goal-side and ball-side of your opponent
Watch the ball and your opponent; do not turn your back
Clear wide and high, away from goal, then push out

rubric.description: 1 = loses the opponent or leaves the zone empty; 3 = holds the job on most corners; 5 = holds the job on every corner and adjusts to the delivery
1 = silent; 3 = calls jobs and claims on most corners; 5 = everyone knows their job from the calls and the keeper commands the area
1 = watches only the ball; 3 = checks ball and opponent on most corners; 5 = keeps ball and opponent in view on every corner

drills.progression: Swap jobs, add a short corner. See sp-007 (zonal, man, hybrid) at 15-16.
drills.video_note: Raised wide view showing each defender's position at the moment of delivery.
drills.safety_note: Goals must be anchored and checked before use. Nobody hangs or swings on the crossbar. No pushing, holding or climbing on opponents.

drills.name: Acceleration Mechanics (0-10m)
drills.description: Short-distance sprint mechanics: forward lean, piston legs, powerful arm drive, and low heel recovery over the first 10 metres.
coaching_points: Push the ground away behind you
Head still, eyes forward, aggressive arms
Full recovery between reps - speed work is not conditioning

rubric.description: 1 = stands up straight and takes long steps at once; 3 = leans forward and drives the arms on most reps; 5 = strong lean, short quick steps and full arm drive on every rep
1 = stops short or jogs through reps; 3 = most reps at a hard pace; 5 = every rep at full effort, all reps done
1 = form breaks after the first few reps; 3 = form holds for most of the set; 5 = form stays the same from first to last rep

drills.progression: Resisted sprints (bands/sled) then contrast with free sprints.
drills.video_note: Side slow-motion of the first 5 steps compared to a reference sprinter.

drills.name: Max Velocity Sprinting
drills.description: Flying sprints (20m build + 20m at max) with tall posture, front-side mechanics, and relaxed rhythm. Low volume, full recovery.
coaching_points: Tall hips, strike under the body
Relax the face and shoulders at top speed
Quality over quantity - stop when speed drops

rubric.description: 1 = tense and bouncing, head shaking; 3 = tall and relaxed for part of the fast section; 5 = tall, relaxed and smooth for the whole fast section
1 = stays at the build pace; 3 = reaches near top speed on most reps; 5 = reaches top speed on every rep, with full rest between
1 = times drop off after rep 2; 3 = times stay close for most reps; 5 = times and form stay the same across all reps

drills.progression: Time with gates or app-based timing; track personal bests per month.
drills.video_note: Side tracking shot at full speed with frame-by-frame contact analysis.

drills.name: Change of Direction (COD) Technique
drills.description: Planned COD patterns (45/90/180-degree cuts, 5-10-5) teaching deceleration, plant mechanics, and re-acceleration.
coaching_points: Brake in short steps, lower the hips before the plant
Plant outside the centre of mass and push away
Eyes up to the next line before you're out of the cut

rubric.description: 1 = stands tall and slides through the turn; 3 = drops the hips and plants on most reps; 5 = slows early, plants low and drives out of every cut
1 = jogs through the pattern; 3 = most cuts at a hard pace; 5 = every cut at full effort
1 = turns well one way only; 3 = both ways, one side slower; 5 = both ways equally clean through the whole set

drills.progression: Progress to reactive versions where the direction is called late.
drills.video_note: Front slow-motion of the plant step; highlight shin angle and hip drop.

drills.name: Reactive Agility (Stimulus-Based)
drills.description: Agility with perception: react to a partner's movement, a called colour, or a light. Trains decision-speed, not just movement speed.
coaching_points: Scan the stimulus while moving
Decelerate under control before redirecting
First step out of the cut must be explosive

rubric.description: 1 = waits and then reacts late; 3 = reacts on most cues and keeps balance; 5 = reacts at once and changes direction with balance, every cue
1 = half-speed reactions; 3 = most reactions at a hard pace; 5 = every reaction at full speed
1 = wrong direction on many cues; 3 = right direction on most cues; 5 = right direction on nearly every cue until the last rep

drills.progression: Mirror drills against a live opponent - closest thing to match agility.
drills.video_note: Clip showing the stimulus and the athlete's response latency.

drills.name: Plyometrics & Landing Mechanics
drills.description: Jump and bound progressions: drop landings, countermovement jumps, hurdle hops, and lateral bounds. Landing quality is trained before jump height.
coaching_points: Land quietly: hips back, knees tracking over toes
Stick the landing before progressing
Full recovery between sets

rubric.description: 1 = knees fall in or the landing is loud and stiff; 3 = soft, quiet landings on most reps; 5 = quiet landings, knees over toes, hips back, every rep
1 = jumps half-height; 3 = most jumps at a hard effort; 5 = every jump at full effort, with full rest
1 = landing quality drops after a few reps; 3 = landing holds for most of the set; 5 = landing quality stays the same to the last rep

drills.progression: Add single-leg variants and reactive jumps off a drop.
drills.video_note: Front and side slow-motion of landings; good vs. valgus collapse comparison.

drills.name: Bodyweight Strength Foundations
drills.description: Fundamental patterns without load: squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull, brace. Circuit or station format, technique-first.
coaching_points: Full range before adding reps
Own the bottom position in squats and lunges
Brace the trunk on every rep

rubric.description: 1 = back rounds or knees collapse; 3 = good shape on most reps with a few cues from the coach; 5 = clean shape on every rep, without a cue
1 = stops early or skips reps; 3 = completes the reps at a steady effort; 5 = completes every rep with full control and effort
1 = shape breaks as the set goes on; 3 = shape holds for most of the set; 5 = shape stays the same from first rep to last

drills.progression: Add tempo (slow eccentrics), pauses, then external load at U16+.
drills.video_note: One clip per pattern from side and front with key positions freeze-framed.

drills.name: Supervised Resistance Training
drills.description: Structured gym programme: trap-bar or goblet squats, RDLs, split squats, presses and rows, with load progression tracked per player.
coaching_points: Qualified supervision mandatory at this age
Technique standard before any load increase
Log every session - progression is the programme

rubric.description: 1 = load too heavy and the shape breaks; 3 = good shape on most reps at the planned load; 5 = clean shape on every rep and a controlled lift and lower
1 = skips sets or reduces the load; 3 = completes the plan; 5 = completes the plan and adds load when the coach says so
1 = logs are missing or the load changes at random; 3 = logs most sessions; 5 = logs every session and the load rises step by step

drills.progression: Individual periodisation aligned to the match calendar.
drills.video_note: Technique reference clip per lift with setup and bar-path cues.
drills.safety_note: Must be designed and supervised by a qualified S&C coach; follow national youth resistance-training guidelines.

drills.name: Core & Stability (Anti-Rotation, Single-Leg)
drills.description: Core as force transfer: plank progressions, Pallof presses, dead bugs, side planks, and single-leg balance/reach work.
coaching_points: Anti-extension and anti-rotation before crunching
Breathe behind the brace
Quality positions - stop when shape breaks

rubric.description: 1 = hips sag or twist; 3 = keeps the body steady for most of each hold; 5 = steady, braced and still for the full hold
1 = skips holds; 3 = completes most holds; 5 = completes every hold at the set time
1 = one side clearly weaker; 3 = both sides, one a little weaker; 5 = both sides equal for every set

drills.progression: Add perturbations (partner band pulls) and unstable single-leg progressions.
drills.video_note: Side and front clips per exercise with common compensation errors shown.

drills.name: Injury-Prevention Block (FIFA 11+, Nordics, Copenhagen)
drills.description: Evidence-based prevention package: FIFA 11+ warm-up structure, Nordic hamstring curls, and Copenhagen adduction, plus ankle/knee control work.
coaching_points: Nordics: control the descent, hips extended
Copenhagen: straight body line, slow tempo
Consistency beats intensity - 2-3x weekly all season

rubric.description: 1 = rushes the moves with poor shape; 3 = right shape on most moves; 5 = slow, controlled, right shape on every move
1 = skips parts of the block; 3 = completes the block; 5 = completes the block with full effort on the hard parts
1 = does it once and stops; 3 = does it most weeks; 5 = does it every session as planned

drills.progression: Progress lever lengths and add load once bodyweight volume is owned.
drills.video_note: Technique clip per exercise with regression and progression shown.
drills.safety_note: Introduce Nordic and Copenhagen volumes gradually to manage soreness.

drills.name: Conditioning Through Small-Sided Games
drills.description: Aerobic and high-intensity conditioning delivered via SSG formats (pitch size and numbers set the load). Ball-present fitness preferred over laps.
coaching_points: Pitch dimensions control the intensity - plan it
Work:rest ratios set the adaptation
Players compete hard: intensity comes from the game

rubric.description: 1 = stands still off the ball; 3 = moves and plays at a steady rate; 5 = moves, plays and presses at the pace the coach set
1 = walks between actions; 3 = works hard for most of each round; 5 = works at full effort in each round and recovers on time
1 = fades in the last rounds; 3 = holds the pace for most rounds; 5 = holds the same pace through the last round

drills.progression: Manipulate format (3v3 large pitch = max intensity; 6v6 small = possession endurance).
drills.video_note: Wide fixed clip of one full bout; overlay work:rest timings.

drills.name: Repeated Sprint Ability (RSA)
drills.description: Repeated maximal or near-maximal sprints (e.g., 6-8 x 30m) on short recovery, straight-line and with a direction change.
coaching_points: Maximal intent on every rep
Incomplete recovery is the point - but form must hold
Track total time and fatigue drop-off

rubric.description: 1 = poor form as soon as tired; 3 = good form on most sprints; 5 = good form on every sprint, including the last
1 = stops or slows by sprint 3; 3 = most sprints at a hard pace; 5 = every sprint at full effort
1 = times fall away by more than 10%; 3 = times drop by about 5%; 5 = times stay within 3% from first sprint to last

drills.progression: Add a ball or a decision at the end of each sprint.
drills.video_note: Clip of the full set with split times overlaid.

drills.name: Mobility & Dynamic Warm-Up Routines
drills.description: Daily mobility block: hip openers, ankle rocks, thoracic rotations, leg swings, and a progressive dynamic warm-up ramp before sessions.
coaching_points: Move with control through full range
Ramp intensity toward the session's first action
Own routine - learn to self-manage

rubric.description: 1 = rushes the moves and skips the range; 3 = right shape on most moves; 5 = full range, slow and smooth on every move
1 = does half the routine; 3 = does the full routine; 5 = does the full routine with focus and in the right order
1 = does it only when told; 3 = does it before most sessions; 5 = does it before every session without being told

drills.progression: Personalise the block per player screening results.
drills.video_note: Follow-along routine video at real speed.

drills.name: Pre-Match Routine & Visualisation
drills.description: Build a repeatable pre-match routine: breathing, visualising 3-5 role-specific success actions, and a one-word focus cue.
coaching_points: Visualise your position's key actions, in first person
Same routine before every match - it becomes a trigger
One cue word for when focus slips

rubric.description: 1 = skips steps or rushes the breathing; 3 = does all steps in the plan; 5 = does all steps calmly and holds the picture clearly
1 = does not use it before a match; 3 = uses it before most matches; 5 = uses it before every match and it is the same each time
1 = says only 'it was fine'; 3 = says what helped and what did not; 5 = says what changed in focus or nerves, and what to try next

drills.progression: Add in-game reset visualisation after reviewing match footage.
drills.video_note: Guided audio-style walkthrough of a full routine.

drills.name: Goal Setting (Process Goals)
drills.description: Set one process goal per training block (e.g., 'scan before every reception') tied to the player's development plan, with a weekly self-check.
coaching_points: Process over outcome: actions you control
Make it observable - a coach could tick it on video
Review weekly, reset monthly

rubric.description: 1 = no goal set; 3 = one goal set that is clear and short; 5 = one clear goal tied to the player's plan, checked every week
1 = goal is not used in training; 3 = uses the goal in some sessions; 5 = uses the goal in every session and shows it in play
1 = no check or it says only yes or no; 3 = says what happened and a reason; 5 = says what happened, why, and the next step

drills.progression: Link goals to rubric scores in the system so progress is measurable.
drills.video_note: Example worksheet walkthrough with good vs. vague goals.

drills.name: Performance Journaling & Self-Review
drills.description: Post-session and post-match written review: what went well, what to improve, one action for next time. Feeds directly into the self-feedback score in your system.
coaching_points: Be specific: name the action, not the feeling
Balance: at least one strength and one improvement
Compare self-review with coach review - discuss the gaps

rubric.description: 1 = writes less than a line or skips sessions; 3 = writes after most sessions; 5 = writes after every session and match, on time
1 = the notes do not change what he does; 3 = uses a note in some sessions; 5 = picks one action from each review and does it next time
1 = only says good or bad; 3 = names what went well and what to fix; 5 = gives clear examples, the cause, and one action

drills.progression: Review monthly trends with the coach; link to individual video clips.
drills.video_note: Example journal entries from real scenarios (anonymised).

drills.name: Sleep, Nutrition & Hydration Foundations
drills.description: Education module: sleep targets for teen athletes (8-10h), pre/post-training fueling basics, hydration habits, and match-day eating timelines.
coaching_points: Sleep is the number-one recovery tool
Fuel before, refuel within an hour after
Build habits, not diets

rubric.description: 1 = does not finish the tasks; 3 = finishes the tasks; 5 = finishes the tasks and asks questions
1 = habits unchanged; 3 = changes one habit; 5 = keeps the new habits for the full block
1 = no record of sleep, food or water; 3 = records most days; 5 = records every day and spots a pattern

drills.progression: Add a weekly habit tracker (sleep hours, hydration) to the player profile.
drills.video_note: Short explainer videos per topic with a quiz checkpoint.

drills.name: Reset Routines: Managing Mistakes
drills.description: Train a 3-second in-game reset after mistakes: exhale, physical trigger (adjust socks/tape), cue word, next-action focus.
coaching_points: Mistakes are information, not identity
The reset must be rehearsed in training, not invented in matches
Next action is the only thing you control

rubric.description: 1 = does not try the routine; 3 = tries the routine in drills; 5 = practises the routine every session
1 = sulks or loses focus after a mistake; 3 = resets in some matches; 5 = resets within three seconds in most matches
1 = cannot say what he did; 3 = says what he did after a mistake; 5 = says what he did, if it worked, and what to change

drills.progression: Coach deliberately creates error scenarios in practice to rehearse resets.
drills.video_note: Examples of elite players visibly using reset triggers.

drills.name: Communication & Leadership Exercises
drills.description: Conditioned games where only designated leaders may talk, rotating the role. Debrief on what information actually helped teammates.
coaching_points: Information beats noise: early, specific, actionable
Leaders organise others, not just themselves
Every player leads in their zone - not just the captain

rubric.description: 1 = stays quiet or talks over others; 3 = takes the role when it is his turn; 5 = takes the role with energy and supports the others
1 = talk is vague and late; 3 = gives clear calls on some plays; 5 = gives short, early, useful calls on most plays
1 = no view on what helped; 3 = names one call that helped; 5 = names which calls helped and why

drills.progression: Assign match-day leadership units (build-up, pressing, set pieces).
drills.video_note: Game clips with audio highlighting effective vs. ineffective communication.
